sentences.zh: 歸崇敬，字正禮，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Gui Chongjing, whose courtesy name was Zhengli, was a man of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Chongjing, courtesy name Zhengli, was a native of Wu in Suzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治禮家學，多識容典，擢明經。

translations.literal: He studied the learning of the ritualist school, was well versed in ceremonial regulations, and was selected through the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: He trained in the ritualist tradition, knew ceremonial codes thoroughly, and passed the Mingjing civil examination.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，孝聞鄉里。

translations.literal: When his father died, his filial conduct became known throughout his home district.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death, his filial devotion won renown in his hometown.

sentences.zh: 調國子直講。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Lecturer at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as a direct lecturer at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，舉博通墳典科，對策第一，遷四門博士。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era he entered the examination for comprehensive mastery of the classical canon; he ranked first in the policy disputation and was promoted to Erudite of the Four Gates.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao period he sat for the broad mastery of the classics examination, took first place in the policy test, and was promoted to Four Gates erudite.

sentences.zh: 有詔舉才可宰百里者，復策高等，授左拾遺。

translations.literal: An edict called for recommending men of talent fit to govern a hundred-li district; he again ranked high in the policy test and was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict sought men capable of governing a county, he again scored highly on the policy examination and was made Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 肅宗次靈武，再遷起居郎、贊善大夫、史館修撰、兼集賢殿校理，修國史、儀註。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong halted at Lingwu, Chongjing was promoted again to Master of the Court Diary, Mentor to the Heir Apparent, Compiler at the Historiography Institute, and concurrently Collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, compiling the national history and ritual commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong made his stand at Lingwu, he was promoted in turn to court diarist, mentor to the heir apparent, historiography compiler, and concurrent collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, working on the national history and ritual regulations.

sentences.zh: 以貧求解。

translations.literal: Because of poverty he requested release from office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his post on account of poverty.

sentences.zh: 歷同州長史、潤州別駕。

translations.literal: He served successively as Chief Administrator of Tongzhou and Vice-Prefect of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive posts as chief administrator of Tongzhou and vice-prefect of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有事橋陵、建陵，召還參掌儀典。

translations.literal: Before long, when rites were to be performed at Qiaoling and Jianling, he was recalled to take part in directing the ceremonial codes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when ceremonies were needed at Qiaoling and Jianling, he was summoned back to help oversee ritual protocol.

sentences.zh: 改主客員外郎，復兼修撰。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions and again served concurrently as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as vice director of the Bureau of Receptions and again held a concurrent compiler post.

sentences.zh: 代宗幸陜，召問得失，崇敬極陳：「生人疲敝，當以儉化天下，則國富而兵可用。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong visited Shanzhou, Chongjing was summoned and asked about the state's strengths and failings. He stated at length: "The people are worn and exhausted; the realm should be transformed through frugality, then the state will be rich and the army can be employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong traveled to Shanzhou, Chongjing was called in to discuss policy. He argued forcefully: "The people are exhausted; frugality must transform the empire, so the state grows wealthy and the army becomes usable again.

sentences.zh: 時百官朝朔望，皆服袴褶，崇敬非之，建言：「三代逮漢無其制，隋以來，始有服者，事不稽古，宜停。」

translations.literal: At that time, when officials attended court on the first and fifteenth of the month, all wore trousers and short jackets. Chongjing disapproved and submitted a memorial: "From the Three Dynasties through Han there was no such practice; only since the Sui has this dress existed. The matter does not accord with antiquity and should be discontinued."
translations.idiomatic: At the time, officials attending the new- and full-moon audiences all wore riding dress. Chongjing objected and proposed: "From the Three Dynasties through Han there was no such custom; only since the Sui has this attire appeared. It has no basis in antiquity and ought to be abolished."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又言：「東都太廟不當置木主，按《禮》：『虞主用桑，練主用栗』，作栗主則瘞桑主，猶天無二日，土無二王也。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Eastern Capital's Imperial Ancestral Temple ought not to keep wooden spirit tablets. According to the Rites: 'The Yu tablet is of mulberry; the Lian tablet is of chestnut.' When the chestnut tablet is made, the mulberry tablet is buried — just as heaven cannot have two suns, earth cannot have two kings.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the Eastern Capital ancestral temple should not house wooden spirit tablets. The Rites state: "The mourning tablet for the Yu rite is mulberry; for the Lian rite, chestnut." Once the chestnut tablet is made, the mulberry tablet is buried — as heaven cannot have two suns, the earth cannot have two sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 東都太廟，本武後所建，以祀諸武，中宗去主存廟，以備行幸遷都之置。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital temple was originally built by Empress Wu to sacrifice to the Wu clan; Emperor Zhongzong removed the tablets but kept the temple, to provide for the emperor's travels and a possible move of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital temple had been built by Empress Wu to honor her clan; Emperor Zhongzong removed the tablets but kept the building in case the court traveled or moved the capital again.

sentences.zh: 且商遷都前八後五，不必每都別立神主也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Shang moved its capital they kept eight tablets before and five after — there was no need to set up separate spirit tablets at every capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shang relocated their capital they retained eight earlier tablets and five later ones — they did not need a separate set of spirit tablets at every site.

sentences.zh: 若曰神主已經奉祀，不得一日而廢，則桑主以虞，至練祭而埋之，明是不然。」

translations.literal: If one says that spirit tablets once enshrined cannot be abolished in a single day, then the mulberry tablet is used for the Yu rite and buried at the Lian sacrifice — which clearly shows that this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: If one claims enshrined tablets cannot be discarded overnight, the mulberry tablet serves only until the Lian rite, when it is buried — which plainly refutes that argument.

sentences.zh: 時有方士巨彭祖建言：「唐家土德，請以四季月郊祀天地。」

translations.literal: At that time the Daoist adept Ju Pengzu proposed: "The Tang house possesses the virtue of Earth; please perform suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth in each of the four seasonal months."
translations.idiomatic: About then the Daoist Ju Pengzu proposed that, since the Tang embodied the virtue of Earth, suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth should be held in each of the four seasonal months.

sentences.zh: 詔禮官儒者雜議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered ritual officials and Confucian scholars to debate the matter together.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered ritual officials and scholars to deliberate jointly.

sentences.zh: 崇敬議：「《禮》以先立秋十八日迎黃靈，祀黃帝，黃帝於五行為土，而火為母，故火用事之末而祭之，三季月則否。

translations.literal: Chongjing argued: "The Rites prescribe that eighteen days before the Beginning of Autumn the Yellow Spirit is welcomed and the Yellow Emperor is sacrificed to. The Yellow Emperor belongs to Earth in the Five Phases, and Fire is its mother; therefore he is worshipped at the end of Fire's season of dominance, not in the other three seasonal months.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjing replied that the Rites call for welcoming the Yellow Spirit and sacrificing to the Yellow Emperor eighteen days before autumn. The Yellow Emperor corresponds to Earth in the five phases, with Fire as its mother, so the rite belongs at the close of Fire's season — not in the other three seasonal months.

sentences.zh: 彭祖牽緯候說，事詭不經，不可用。」

translations.literal: Pengzu relied on apocryphal prognostic texts; the proposal was bizarre and unorthodox and could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Pengzu's argument rested on omen lore and prognostic texts — an eccentric, unsound proposal that should be rejected.

sentences.zh: 又議：「五人帝於國家為前後，無君臣義，天子祭宜毋稱臣，祭而稱臣，於天帝無異。」

translations.literal: He also argued: "The Five Emperors stand before and after the state in succession; there is no relationship of ruler and subject. When the Son of Heaven sacrifices, he ought not call himself subject. To sacrifice while calling oneself subject is no different from doing so to the Lord on High."
translations.idiomatic: He also held that the Five Emperors precede and succeed the dynasty without a subject–ruler bond, so the Son of Heaven should not style himself their subject in sacrifice — to do so would blur the distinction owed to Heaven itself.

sentences.zh: 又：「春秋釋奠孔子，祝版皇帝署，北面揖，以為太重。

translations.literal: He also said: "At the spring and autumn libation sacrifices to Confucius, the prayer text bears the emperor's signature and he bows facing north — this is, in my view, excessively deferential.
translations.idiomatic: He also objected that at the spring and autumn Confucian sacrifices the prayer tablet bears the emperor's name while he bows facing north — an excessive show of deference.

sentences.zh: 宜準武王受丹書於師尚父，行東面之禮。」

translations.literal: It would be proper to follow King Wu receiving the red writ from Master Father Shang and perform the rite facing east."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed following King Wu, who received the red writ from the Grand Mentor while facing east — the emperor should face east in the rite.

sentences.zh: 事皆施行。

translations.literal: All these measures were put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: These recommendations were all adopted.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，授倉部郎中，充吊祭冊立新羅使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era he was appointed Director in the Bureau of Granaries and commissioned as envoy to offer condolences, perform sacrifices, and invest the new king of Silla.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dali era he became director in the Bureau of Granaries and served as envoy to mourn, sacrifice, and invest Silla's new king.

sentences.zh: 海道風濤，舟幾壞，眾驚，謀以單舸載而免，答曰：「今共舟數十百人，我何忍獨濟哉？」

translations.literal: On the sea route wind and waves arose; the ship was nearly lost. The company panicked and planned to escape by loading him alone into a small boat. He replied: "There are now several tens or hundreds of people on this ship — how could I bear to cross alone?
translations.idiomatic: At sea a storm nearly wrecked the ship. When others panicked and proposed putting him alone in a skiff to save him, he said: "There are scores of us aboard — how could I save myself alone?

sentences.zh: 少選，風息。

translations.literal: Before long the wind died down.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the wind fell.

sentences.zh: 先是，使外國多賫金帛，貿舉所無，崇敬囊橐惟衾衣，東夷傳其清德。

translations.literal: Previously, envoys to foreign states often brought gold and silk to trade for local goods; Chongjing's bags held only bedding and clothing, and the eastern barbarians spread word of his pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys abroad had usually carried gold and silk to buy local goods, but Chongjing traveled with only bedding and clothes, and eastern peoples praised his integrity far and wide.

sentences.zh: 還，授國子司業、兼集賢學士。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and concurrently Academician at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he became vice director of the Imperial University and concurrent academician at the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 八年，遣祀衡山，未至，而哥舒晃亂廣州，監察御史憚之，請望祀而還，崇敬正色曰：「君命豈有畏邪？」

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was sent to sacrifice at Mount Heng. Before he arrived, Geshu Huang rebelled at Guangzhou. The investigating censor feared this and asked to perform a distant sacrifice and return. Chongjing said sternly: "How can one shrink from an imperial commission?
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was dispatched to sacrifice at Mount Heng. Before he arrived, Geshu Huang rebelled in Guangzhou. The investigating censor, afraid, asked to offer a distant sacrifice and turn back. Chongjing said gravely: "How can one fear an imperial command?

sentences.zh: 遂往。

translations.literal: He went on.
translations.idiomatic: He proceeded as ordered.

sentences.zh: 皇太子欲臨國學行齒胄禮，崇敬以學與官名皆不正，乃建議：

translations.literal: The Crown Prince wished to visit the Directorate of Education to perform the ceremony of ordering caps by age. Chongjing held that both the school's name and its official titles were incorrect, and submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince wished to visit the Imperial University for the cap-ordering ceremony, Chongjing argued that both the institution's name and its offices were improper and submitted a detailed proposal:

sentences.zh: 古天子學曰辟雍。

translations.literal: The ancient Son of Heaven's school was called Piyong.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's ancient academy was called Piyong.

sentences.zh: 以制言之，壅水環繚如璧然；

translations.literal: In terms of its form, encircling water was banked round like a jade disc;
translations.idiomatic: In architectural terms, its encircling moat was banked like a round jade disc;

sentences.zh: 以誼言之，以禮樂明和天下云爾。

translations.literal: in terms of its meaning, rites and music made clear harmony under Heaven — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: in meaning, rites and music clarified harmony throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 在《禮》為澤宮，故前世或曰璧池，或曰璧沼，亦言學省。

translations.literal: In the Rites it is called the Marsh Palace; hence earlier ages sometimes called it the Jade Pool or Jade Marsh, and also spoke of the School Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites call it the Marsh Palace; earlier ages also named it the Jade Pool or Jade Marsh, and referred to the school directorate.

sentences.zh: 漢光武立明堂、辟雍、靈臺，號「三雍宮」。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu of Han established the Bright Hall, Piyong, and Spirit Terrace, calling them the "Three Yong Palaces."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu of Han built the Bright Hall, Piyong, and Spirit Terrace, collectively termed the Three Yong Palaces.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝臨辟雍，行鄉飲酒禮，別立國子學，以殊士庶。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin visited Piyong and performed the district drinking ceremony; he separately established the Directorate of the Heir Apparent's Sons to distinguish gentlemen from commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin visited Piyong for the district drinking rite and separately founded the Imperial University to distinguish elite students from commoners.

sentences.zh: 永嘉南遷，唯有國子學。

translations.literal: When the court moved south at Yongjia, only the Directorate of the Heir Apparent's Sons remained.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia flight south, only the Imperial University survived.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，更名國子監。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui it was renamed the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui Daye reign it was renamed the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 今聲明之盛，辟雍獨闕，請以國子監為辟雍省。

translations.literal: Now in this age of brilliant renown Piyong alone is missing; I ask that the Directorate of Education be made the Piyong Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In our present age of cultural brilliance Piyong alone is absent; he proposed renaming the Directorate of Education the Piyong Directorate.

sentences.zh: 祭酒、司業之名，非學官所宜。

translations.literal: The titles Director of Libations and Vice Director are not fitting for school officials.
translations.idiomatic: The titles Director of Libations and Vice Director were unsuitable for academic officers.

sentences.zh: 業者，栒虡大版，今學不教樂，於義無當。

translations.literal: "Ye" refers to the great sounding-board of the bell-stand; today the school does not teach music, so the term is inappropriate in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: "Ye" denoted the great sounding-board on the bell frame, yet the school no longer taught music, so the title no longer fit.

sentences.zh: 請以祭酒為太師氏，位三品；

translations.literal: I ask that the Director of Libations be made Grand Master, rank third class;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed renaming the director of libations Grand Master, third rank;

sentences.zh: 司業為左師、右師，位四品。

translations.literal: and the Vice Director be made Left Master and Right Master, rank fourth class.
translations.idiomatic: and the vice director Left Master and Right Master, fourth rank.

sentences.zh: 近世明經，不課其義，先取帖經，顓門廢業，傳受義絕。

translations.literal: In recent times the Mingjing examination did not test understanding of meaning but first required copying passages; specialized schools abandoned their studies and the transmission of exegesis ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Mingjing exam tested rote copying rather than meaning; specialized schools withered and the transmission of classical interpretation died out.

sentences.zh: 請以《禮記》、《左氏春秋》為大經，《周官》、《儀禮》、《毛詩》為中經，《尚書》、《周易》為小經，各置博士一員。

translations.literal: I ask that the Record of Rites and Mr. Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals be made great classics; the Rites of Zhou, Ceremonial Rites, and Mao's Odes middle classics; the Documents and Changes small classics — with one erudite appointed for each.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed classing the Record of Rites and Zuo's Annals as major classics; the Rites of Zhou, Etiquette, and Mao's Odes as middle classics; the Documents and Changes as minor classics — each with its own erudite.

sentences.zh: 《公羊》、《穀梁春秋》共準一中經，通置博士一員。

translations.literal: The Gongyang and Guliang commentaries on the Spring and Autumn should jointly count as one middle classic, with one erudite appointed for both.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyang and Guliang commentaries would jointly count as one middle classic under a single erudite.

sentences.zh: 博士兼通《孝經》、《論語》，依章疏講解。

translations.literal: Erudites should also be versed in the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects, lecturing according to chapter commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites would also teach the Classic of Filial Piety and Analects from standard commentaries.

sentences.zh: 德行純絜、文詞雅正、形容莊重可為師表者，委四品以上各舉所知，在外給傳，七十者安車蒲輪敦遣。

translations.literal: Men of pure conduct, elegant diction, and dignified bearing fit to be models for students should be recommended by officials of fourth rank and above, each naming those they knew; those outside the capital were given travel passes, and men of seventy were sent carriage and wheel-wrapped summons with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of pure conduct, refined style, and dignified bearing fit to be models would be recommended by officials of fourth rank and above; those in the provinces would receive travel documents, and men of seventy would be summoned with honor in cushioned carriages.

sentences.zh: 國子、太學、四門三館，各立五經博士，品秩、生徒有差。

translations.literal: The three schools — Directorate of the Heir Apparent's Sons, Grand Academy, and Four Gates — should each establish erudites for the Five Classics, with differences in rank and number of students.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University, Grand Academy, and Four Gates would each appoint Five Classics erudites, with differing ranks and enrollments.

sentences.zh: 舊博士、助教、直講、經直、律館、算館助教，請皆罷。

translations.literal: The former posts of erudite, assistant instructor, direct lecturer, classics supervisor, and assistant instructors in the law and computation halls should all be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed abolishing the old posts of erudite, assistant instructor, direct lecturer, classics supervisor, and law- and computation-hall assistants.

sentences.zh: 教授法。

translations.literal: Regulations for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching regulations.

sentences.zh: 學生謁師，贄用暇脩一束、酒一壺、衫布一裁，色如師所服。

translations.literal: When students paid their first visit to a teacher, the gift consisted of a bundle of dried meat, a flask of wine, and a length of garment cloth matching the teacher's color.
translations.idiomatic: On first meeting a teacher, students would present dried meat, wine, and a length of cloth dyed to match the teacher's robe.

sentences.zh: 師出中門，延入與坐，割脩奭斗酒，三爵止。

translations.literal: The teacher came out through the middle gate, received the student, and sat with him; they shared the dried meat and exchanged a cup of wine, stopping after three rounds.
translations.idiomatic: The teacher would come to the middle gate, invite the student in, share the meat and exchange cups of wine, stopping after three rounds.

sentences.zh: 乃發篋出經，摳衣前請，師為說經大略，然後就室，朝晡請益。

translations.literal: Then the case was opened and the classic brought out; the student gathered his robe and advanced to request instruction, and the teacher explained the general purport of the classic. Afterward the student entered the study and sought further instruction morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: The teacher would then open the case, bring out the classic, and outline its meaning at the student's request before the student entered the study for morning and evening lessons.

sentences.zh: 師二時堂上訓授道義，示以文行忠信、孝悌睦友。

translations.literal: Twice daily in the hall the teacher instructed in the Way and its meaning, showing culture, conduct, loyalty, faithfulness, filial piety, fraternal duty, and harmonious friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Twice daily in the lecture hall the teacher would expound the Way and exemplify culture, conduct, loyalty, trustworthiness, filial piety, brotherliness, and amity.

sentences.zh: 旬省、月試、時考、歲貢，視生徒及第多少為博士考課上下。

translations.literal: Decennial review, monthly tests, seasonal examinations, and annual presentation — the number of students who passed would determine the erudite's rating as superior or inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Decennial reviews, monthly tests, seasonal exams, and annual presentations would rate erudites by how many students passed.

sentences.zh: 有不率教者，槚楚之，國子移禮部，為太學生；

translations.literal: Those who did not follow instruction were beaten with the rod; students of the Directorate were transferred through the Ministry of Rites to become students of the Grand Academy;
translations.idiomatic: Students who disobeyed would be caned; Imperial University students would be demoted via the Ministry of Rites to the Grand Academy;

sentences.zh: 太學又不變，徙之四門；

translations.literal: if they still did not reform in the Grand Academy, they were moved to the Four Gates;
translations.idiomatic: if they still failed to reform at the Grand Academy, to the Four Gates;

sentences.zh: 四門不變，徙本州之學；

translations.literal: if they did not reform at the Four Gates, they were sent to their home prefecture's school;
translations.idiomatic: if they still did not reform at the Four Gates, to their home prefecture's school;

sentences.zh: 復不變，繇役如初，終身不齒。

translations.literal: if they still did not reform, they were returned to corvée labor as before and never again ranked among students.
translations.idiomatic: and if they still did not reform, they would return to corvée labor and never again be counted among students.

sentences.zh: 雖率教，九年學不成者，亦歸之本州。

translations.literal: Even those who followed instruction, if after nine years they had not completed their studies, were also sent back to their home prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Even obedient students who failed to finish after nine years would be sent home to their prefectures.

sentences.zh: 禮部考試法。

translations.literal: Examination regulations of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites examination regulations.

sentences.zh: 請罷帖經，於所習經問大義二十而得十八，《論語》、《孝經》十得八，為通；

translations.literal: I ask that copying passages be abolished; on the classic studied, twenty questions on great meaning with eighteen correct, and on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety ten with eight correct, shall count as passing;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed ending the copy-from-memory test: twenty questions on the major meaning of one's classic with eighteen correct, and ten on the Analects and Classic of Filial Piety with eight correct, would constitute a pass;

sentences.zh: 策三道，以本經對，通二為及第。

translations.literal: three policy questions answered from one's own classic — passing two would constitute attaining the degree.
translations.idiomatic: plus three policy questions answered from one's own classic, with two correct answers required for a degree.

sentences.zh: 其孝行聞鄉里者，舉解具言，試日義闕一二，許兼收焉。

translations.literal: Those whose filial conduct was known in their home district should have it stated fully in the recommendation; on the day of the examination, if they fell short by one or two answers on meaning, they might still be admitted together.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates renowned for filial piety in their districts would be fully described in recommendations, and on exam day might pass despite one or two missed answers on meaning.

sentences.zh: 天下鄉貢如之。

translations.literal: District recommendations throughout the realm would follow the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial recommendations nationwide would follow the same rules.

sentences.zh: 習業考試，並以明經為名，得第授官，與進士同。

translations.literal: Study and examinations would all be called Mingjing; those who attained the degree would receive office on the same terms as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Academic study and examinations would all fall under the Mingjing title, and degree holders would receive office equal to jinshi graduates.

sentences.zh: 有詔尚書省集百官議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to assemble all officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Department of State Affairs to convene officials for debate.

sentences.zh: 皆以習俗久，制度難分明，省禁非外司所宜名，《周官》世職者稱氏，國學非世官，不得名辟雍省、太師氏。

translations.literal: All held that custom was long established and the regulations hard to distinguish; directorates and prohibitions were not names outer offices should use; in the Rites of Zhou hereditary offices were called clans, but the Directorate of Education was not a hereditary office and could not be named Piyong Directorate or Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: All argued that long-standing custom made the reforms hard to distinguish, that directorate titles were inappropriate for outer offices, and that since only hereditary offices in the Rites of Zhou bore clan titles, the Imperial University could not be renamed Piyong Directorate or Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 大抵憚改作，故無施行者。

translations.literal: For the most part they feared innovation, and therefore none of it was put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Most officials feared innovation, so none of his reforms was adopted.

sentences.zh: 坐史給稟錢不實，貶饒州司馬。

translations.literal: Because the clerks' disbursement of grain money was found false, he was demoted to Militia Commandant of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks' grain stipends were found falsified, he was demoted to militia commandant of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，召還，復拜國子司業，稍遷翰林學士、左散騎常侍，充皇太子侍讀，又兼晉王元帥參謀，封餘姚郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong acceded, Chongjing was recalled and again appointed Vice Director of the Directorate of Education; he was gradually promoted to Hanlin Academician and Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, served as Reader to the Crown Prince, and concurrently Staff Officer to the Prince of Jin as commander-in-chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Yuyao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Chongjing was recalled as vice director of the Imperial University, then rose to Hanlin academician and left regular attendant, reader to the crown prince, and staff officer to the Prince of Jin as commander-in-chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 田悅、李納稟命，持節宣慰，稱旨。

translations.literal: When Tian Yue and Li Na submitted to orders, he was sent with staff of authority to proclaim consolation and pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yue and Li Na submitted, he was dispatched with imperial staff to offer consolation and won the emperor's approval.

sentences.zh: 表歸上冢，寵賜繒帛，儒生以為榮。

translations.literal: He memorialized to return and visit his ancestors' tombs; the emperor favored him with gifts of silk, and Confucian scholars took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to visit his family tombs; the emperor bestowed silk gifts, which scholars regarded as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書，仍前職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works while retaining his former duties.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of works while keeping his previous posts.

sentences.zh: 年老，以兵部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: In old age he retired as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he retired as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十八，贈尚書左僕射，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-eight; posthumously he was given the title of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-eight and was posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 論撰數十篇。

translations.literal: He composed several tens of treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote several dozen essays.

sentences.zh: 子登。

translations.literal: His son was Deng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Deng.

sentences.zh: 崇敬子 登登，字沖之，事繼母篤孝。

translations.literal: Chongjing's son Deng — Deng, whose courtesy name was Chongzhi, was deeply filial toward his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjing's son Deng, courtesy name Chongzhi, was devoted in filial service to his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，舉孝廉高第。

translations.literal: In the Dali era he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and ranked high.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and ranked at the top.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，策賢良，為右拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he passed the examination for Worthy and Good and was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era he passed the Worthy and Good examination and became Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡得幸，德宗欲遂以相，右補闕熊執易疏論之，以示登，登動容曰：「願竄吾名，雷霆之下，君難獨處。」

translations.literal: When Pei Yanling won favor and Dezong wished to make him chancellor, Right Supplementation Censor Xiong Zhiyi submitted a memorial opposing it and showed it to Deng. Deng's expression changed as he said: "I beg you to add my name. Under the thunder, how can you stand alone?
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Yanling won favor and Dezong meant to make him chancellor, Right Supplementation Censor Xiong Zhiyi memorialized against it and showed Deng the draft. Deng's face changed: "Put my name on it — under the emperor's wrath you should not stand alone.

sentences.zh: 故同列有所諫正，輒聯署無所回諱。

translations.literal: Hence whenever colleagues offered remonstrance, he would join in signing without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever colleagues submitted remonstrances, he co-signed without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 轉右補闕、起居舍人，凡十五年，僚類有出其下而進趨，自喜得顯官，惟登與右拾遺蔣武退然遠權勢，終不以淹晚概懷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Supplementation Censor and Master of the Court Diary; for fifteen years in all, colleagues who had ranked below him advanced and rejoiced in obtaining prominent office. Only Deng and Right Reminder Jiang Wu quietly kept their distance from power and never resented their late advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Supplementation Censor and court diarist. For fifteen years colleagues who had once ranked below him advanced and exulted in high office, but only Deng and Right Reminder Jiang Wu quietly kept away from power and never resented their slow promotion.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 順宗為皇太子，登父子侍讀，及即位，以東宮恩超拜給事中，遷工部侍郎，復為皇太子、諸王侍讀，獻《龍樓箴》以諷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong was crown prince, Deng served as reader to him; when Shunzong acceded, because of Eastern Palace favor Deng was promoted by special appointment to Palace Attendant, then Vice Minister of Works, and again served as reader to the crown prince and princes, presenting the Admonition of the Dragon Tower as remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong was crown prince, Deng served as his reader; on Shunzong's accession, Deng was specially promoted to palace attendant, then vice minister of works, and again reader to the crown prince and imperial princes, presenting the Admonition of the Dragon Tower as counsel.

sentences.zh: 徙左散騎常侍，入謝。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and entered to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left regular attendant of the cavalry and went in to thank the emperor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗問政所先，登知帝睿而果於斷，勸順納諫爭，內外傳為讜言。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong asked what should come first in government. Deng knew the emperor was perceptive and decisive in judgment; he urged compliance and acceptance of remonstrance, and inside and outside the court this was spread as forthright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong asked what should come first in governing. Knowing the emperor was sharp and decisive, Deng urged obedience and openness to remonstrance; court and capital alike praised his frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 後判國子祭酒事，進工部尚書，累封長洲縣男。

translations.literal: Later he served concurrently as Director of Libations of the Directorate of Education, was promoted to Minister of Works, and was enfeoffed cumulatively as Baron of Changzhou county.
translations.idiomatic: He later acted as director of libations at the Imperial University, rose to minister of works, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十七，贈太子少師，謚曰憲。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-seven; posthumously he was given the title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven and was posthumously made junior mentor to the heir apparent, with the posthumous name Xian.

sentences.zh: 登性溫恕，家僮為馬所踶，笞折馬足，登知，不加責。

translations.literal: Deng's nature was mild and forgiving. A household servant was kicked by a horse; he beat the horse and broke its leg. When Deng learned of it, he did not punish the servant.
translations.idiomatic: Deng was gentle and forgiving. When a servant was kicked by a horse and beat the animal until its leg broke, Deng learned of it but did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 有遺金石不死藥者，紿曰已嘗，及登服幾死，訊之，乃未之嘗，人皆為怒，而登不為慍。

translations.literal: Someone presented him with a mineral elixir of immortality; he deceived them by saying he had already tried it. When Deng took it he nearly died. On inquiry it turned out he had never tried it; everyone was angry on his behalf, but Deng showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Someone gave him a mineral elixir of immortality; he lied that he had already tried it. When Deng took it he nearly died. Questioning revealed he had never tasted it; others were furious on his behalf, but Deng showed no anger.

sentences.zh: 常慕陸象先為人，世亦許其類云。

translations.literal: He always admired Lu Xiangxian as a man, and the age also acknowledged him as of that kind.
translations.idiomatic: He always admired Lu Xiangxian's character, and his contemporaries agreed he was much the same.

sentences.zh: 子融。

translations.literal: His son was Rong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rong.

sentences.zh: 登子 融融，字章之，元和中，及進士第，累遷左拾遺。

translations.literal: Deng's son Rong — Rong, whose courtesy name was Zhangzhi — in the Yuanhe era passed the jinshi examination and was promoted cumulatively to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Deng's son Rong, courtesy name Zhangzhi, passed the jinshi examination in the Yuanhe era and rose to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 事文宗為翰林學士，進至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served Emperor Wenzong as Hanlin Academician and rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wenzong he served as a Hanlin academician and rose to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 開成初，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaicheng era he was appointed Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng era he was made vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 湖南觀察使盧周仁以南方屢火，取羨錢億萬進京師。

translations.literal: Hunan Observation Commissioner Lu Zhouren, citing repeated fires in the south, took surplus funds amounting to hundreds of millions and presented them at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhouren, observation commissioner of Hunan, citing repeated fires in the south, sent surplus funds worth hundreds of millions to the capital.

sentences.zh: 融劾奏：「天下一家，中外之財皆陛下府庫。

translations.literal: Rong memorialized in impeachment: "Under Heaven there is one family; wealth within and without are all in Your Majesty's treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Rong impeached him, arguing: "The realm is one household; all wealth at home and abroad belongs in Your Majesty's treasury.

sentences.zh: 周仁陳小利，假異端，公違詔書，徇私希恩。

translations.literal: Zhouren presented minor profits under false pretexts, openly violating edicts, seeking favor through private interest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouren offered petty profits under false pretexts, openly defying imperial edicts to curry favor through private interest.

sentences.zh: 恐海內效之，因緣漁刻，生人受弊，罪始周仁。

translations.literal: I fear the realm will imitate this, using pretexts to extort, and the living will suffer harm — the crime begins with Zhouren.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the empire will follow his example, extorting under one pretext or another until the people suffer — and the fault will begin with Zhouren.

sentences.zh: 請重責，還所進，代貧民租入。」

translations.literal: I ask heavy punishment, return what was presented, and use it for poor people's tax payments.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be punished severely, that the tribute be returned, and that it be applied to poor people's tax payments.

sentences.zh: 詔不從，置錢河陰院以虞水旱。

translations.literal: The edict did not follow his advice; the money was placed in the Heyin depot against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept his proposal and instead placed the funds in the Heyin depot as a reserve against flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 初，戶部員外郎盧元中、左司員外郎判戶部案姚康受平糴官秦季元絹六千匹，貸乾沒錢八千萬，俱貶嶺南尉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Director Lu Yuanzhong of the Ministry of Revenue and Vice Director Yao Kang of the Left Section, who handled revenue cases, had accepted six thousand bolts of silk from grain-purchase official Qin Jiyuan and loaned eighty million in embezzled funds; both were demoted to military aides in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lu Yuanzhong, vice director in the Ministry of Revenue, and Yao Kang of the Left Section, who handled revenue cases, had accepted six thousand bolts of silk from grain-purchase official Qin Jiyuan and loaned out eighty million in embezzled funds; both were demoted to military aides in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 數年，金部員外郎韓益判度支，子弟受賕三百萬，未入者半。

translations.literal: Several years later, Vice Director Han Yi of the Bureau of Metals judged the Revenue Commission; his sons and younger brothers accepted bribes of three million, half not yet received.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Han Yi of the Bureau of Metals oversaw the Revenue Commission; his sons and younger brothers had accepted three million in bribes, half of which had not yet been paid.

sentences.zh: 帝問融：「益所犯與盧元中、姚康孰甚？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Rong: "Whose offense is graver — Yi's, or Lu Yuanzhong's and Yao Kang's?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Rong: "Is Yi's offense graver than those of Lu Yuanzhong and Yao Kang?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「元中等枉失庫錢，益所坐子弟受賄，事異法輕。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Yuanzhong and the others wrongly lost treasury funds; Yi is guilty because his sons and younger brothers took bribes — the cases differ and the law is lighter."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Yuanzhong and the others misappropriated treasury funds; Yi is guilty because his sons and younger brothers took bribes — different cases, and the lighter penalty applies."

sentences.zh: 故益止貶梧州參軍。

translations.literal: Therefore Yi was only demoted to militia aide in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was therefore demoted only to militia aide in Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 融遷京兆尹，李固言為相，惡之，徙秘書監。

translations.literal: Rong was transferred to metropolitan magistrate; Li Guyin as chancellor disliked him and moved him to Director of the Imperial Archives.
translations.idiomatic: Rong became metropolitan magistrate, but Chancellor Li Guyin disliked him and transferred him to director of the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 固言罷，擢權知兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Guyin left office, Rong was promoted to acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After Guyin left office, Rong was promoted to acting vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 歲間，出為山南西道節度使，徙東川。

translations.literal: Within the year he went out as military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, then was transferred to Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year he was posted as military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit, then transferred to Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 還，歷兵部尚書，累封晉陵郡公。

translations.literal: On his return he served as Minister of War and was cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Jinling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he served as minister of war and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 會昌後，儒臣少，朝廷禮典多本融議。

translations.literal: After Huichang, Confucian officials were few, and many court ritual codes drew on Rong's proposals.
translations.idiomatic: After the Huichang era, Confucian officials were scarce, and many court rituals followed Rong's proposals.

sentences.zh: 辭疾，以太子少傅分司東都。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and became Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent stationed at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned citing illness and became junior mentor to the heir apparent at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 大中七年，卒，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dazhong he died and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dazhong he died and was posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 奚陟，字殷卿，其先自譙亳西徙，故為京兆人。

translations.literal: Xi Chi, whose courtesy name was Yinqing; his ancestors had moved west from Qiao and Bo, so he was reckoned a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chi, courtesy name Yinqing, came from a family that had moved west from Qiao and Bo, and was therefore counted as a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少篤誌，通群書。

translations.literal: In youth he was deeply committed in purpose and mastered many books.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was deeply serious in purpose and mastered a wide range of books.

sentences.zh: 大歷末，擢進士、文辭清麗科，授弘文館校書郎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali era he passed the jinshi examination and the examination for elegant literary compositions, and was appointed Collator at the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Dali era he passed the jinshi and elegant literary composition examinations and was appointed collator at the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，諫議大夫崔河圖持節使吐蕃，表陟自副，以親老辭不拜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong acceded, Remonstrance and Advice Grandee Cui Hetu went as envoy to Tibet with staff of authority and recommended Xi as his deputy; Xi declined the appointment because his parents were old.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong took the throne, Remonstrance and Advice Grandee Cui Hetu went as envoy to Tibet and recommended Xi as his deputy; Xi declined because his parents were elderly.

sentences.zh: 楊炎輔政，召授左拾遺。

translations.literal: When Yang Yan assisted in government, Xi was summoned and appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yan came to power, Xi was summoned and appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，毀瘠過禮。

translations.literal: While in mourning for a parent, his emaciation exceeded what ritual required.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning a parent, he grew so emaciated that he exceeded ritual norms.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，走間道及車駕於興元，拜起居郎、翰林學士，不就職。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Xi traveled by back roads and reached the imperial carriage at Xingyuan; he was appointed Master of the Court Diary and Hanlin Academician but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Xi traveled by back roads to join the imperial carriage at Xingyuan and was appointed court diarist and Hanlin academician, but did not take up the posts.

sentences.zh: 賊平，改太子司議郎，歷金部、吏部員外。

translations.literal: After the rebels were pacified, he was changed to Secretary to the Crown Prince's Household and served successively as Vice Director in the Bureaus of Metals and Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, he became secretary to the crown prince's household and then served as vice director in the Bureaus of Metals and Personnel.

sentences.zh: 會左右丞缺，轉左司郎中。

translations.literal: When there was a vacancy among the left and right vice directors, he was made Left Section Director.
translations.idiomatic: When a vacancy opened among the left and right vice directors, he was made left section director.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan he was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenyuan he was promoted to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 於是江南、淮西皆大水，詔陟勞問循慰，所至人人便安。

translations.literal: Then both south of the Yangzi and west of the Huai suffered great floods; an edict sent Xi to comfort and console the people, and wherever he went everyone was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When both the Jiangnan and Huai west regions suffered major floods, an edict sent Xi to comfort the people, and wherever he went the populace was reassured.

sentences.zh: 中書吏倚宰相勢，常姑息，獨陟遇之無假借。

translations.literal: Secretariat clerks relied on the chancellor's power and were usually indulged; only Xi would not grant them license.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat clerks usually relied on the chancellor's power and were indulged; Xi alone refused to grant them any license.

sentences.zh: 先是，右省雜給氐職田稟，主事與拾遺等，陟以奉稍為率，由是吏官有差。

translations.literal: Previously the right secretariat's miscellaneous allowances of Di office land grain were shared among chief clerks and remonstrators alike; Xi used the director's salary as the standard, and thereafter offices and clerks had clear distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the right secretariat's miscellaneous grain allowances from Di office lands had been shared equally among chief clerks and remonstrators; Xi used the director's salary as the standard, establishing clear distinctions among offices and clerks.

sentences.zh: 中書令李晟有紙筆猥料積於省，它日以遺舍人，而雜事舍人常私有之，陟均舍寮無厚薄。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Sheng had accumulated paper and brush supplies in the secretariat; one day he meant to give them to the drafters, but miscellaneous affairs drafters often kept them privately; Xi distributed them equally among all drafters without favor.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Sheng had accumulated paper and brush supplies in the secretariat; when he meant to give them to the drafters, miscellaneous affairs drafters often kept them for themselves — Xi distributed them equally among all drafters without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 雖細務，皆身親其勞，久益強力，人以為難。

translations.literal: Even in minor matters he personally took on the labor; over time he grew ever more vigorous — people considered this difficult to match.
translations.idiomatic: Even in minor matters he took on the work himself; over time he grew ever more vigorous, which people found hard to match.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹李充有美政，裴延齡惡之，誣劾充比陸贄，數遺金帛，當抵罪，又乾沒京兆錢六十八萬緡，請付比部鉤校。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Magistrate Li Chong had excellent administration; Pei Yanling hated him and falsely impeached Chong for associating with Lu Zan and repeatedly sending him gold and silk, deserving punishment, and for embezzling 680,000 strings of metropolitan funds, asking that the case be sent to the audit bureau for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan magistrate Li Chong governed well; Pei Yanling hated him and falsely impeached him for associating with Lu Zan and repeatedly sending him gold and silk, for which he deserved punishment, and for embezzling 680,000 strings of metropolitan funds, asking the audit bureau to investigate.

sentences.zh: 時郎中崔元翰怨贄，揣延齡指，逮系搒掠甚急，內以險文。

translations.literal: At the time Section Director Cui Yuanhan bore a grudge against Zan and, guessing Yanling's intent, pursued the case with extreme beating and interrogation, using treacherous wording within.
translations.idiomatic: Section Director Cui Yuanhan, who bore a grudge against Zan, guessed Yanling's intent and pursued the case with brutal beating and interrogation, using treacherous wording in the record.

sentences.zh: 陟持平無所上下，具獄上，且言：「京兆錢給縣館傳，余以度支符用度略盡。」

translations.literal: Xi maintained balance without favoring either side, submitted the full case to the throne, and said: "Metropolitan funds supply county hostels and courier stations; the remainder was nearly exhausted through revenue commission warrants.
translations.idiomatic: Xi maintained impartiality, submitted the full case, and explained: "Metropolitan funds supply county hostels and courier stations; the remainder was nearly exhausted through revenue commission warrants.

sentences.zh: 充既免，元翰不得意，以恚死。

translations.literal: Chong was exonerated; Yuanhan, dissatisfied, died of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was exonerated; Yuanhan, frustrated, died of resentment.

sentences.zh: 陟尋知吏部選事，遷侍郎。

translations.literal: Xi soon took charge of personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel and was promoted to Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xi soon took charge of personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel and was promoted to vice minister.

sentences.zh: 銓綜平允，時謂與李朝隱略等，不能擿發清明如裴行儉、盧從願也。

translations.literal: His evaluations were fair and even; contemporaries said he was roughly equal to Li Chaoyin but could not discern and promote the clear-sighted as Pei Xingjian and Lu Congyuan had.
translations.idiomatic: His evaluations were fair and even; contemporaries said he was roughly on par with Li Chaoyin but could not discover and promote talent as clearly as Pei Xingjian and Lu Congyuan had.

sentences.zh: 十五年，病癰，帝遣醫療視，敕曰：「陟，賢臣，為我善治之。」

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he fell ill with carbuncle; the emperor sent physicians to treat him and ordered: "Xi is a worthy minister — treat him well for me.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he fell ill with a carbuncle; the emperor sent physicians and ordered: "Xi is a worthy minister — treat him well for me.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-five and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five and was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 陟少自底厲，著名節。

translations.literal: From youth Xi disciplined himself and was famed for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xi disciplined himself and was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 常薦權德輿為起居舍人知制誥，楊於陵為郎中，其後皆有名。

translations.literal: He often recommended Quan Deyu as court diarist drafting edicts and Yang Yuling as section director; both later achieved renown.
translations.idiomatic: He often recommended Quan Deyu as court diarist drafting edicts and Yang Yuling as section director; both later won renown.

sentences.zh: 子敬玄，位左補闕。

translations.literal: His son Jingxuan held the post of Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxuan served as Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 崔衍，字著，深州安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Yan, whose courtesy name was Zhuo, was a man of Anping in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yan, courtesy name Zhuo, was from Anping in Shen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父倫，字敘，居父喪，跣護柩行千里，道路為流涕，廬冢彌年。

translations.literal: His father Lun, courtesy name Xu, while in mourning for his father went barefoot guarding the coffin for a thousand li; passersby wept on the road, and he dwelt in a mourning hut by the tomb for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lun, courtesy name Xu, while mourning his father went barefoot guarding the coffin for a thousand li; travelers wept along the road, and he lived in a mourning hut by the tomb for a full year.

sentences.zh: 服除，及進士第，歷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he passed the jinshi examination and served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he passed the jinshi examination and served as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，陷於賊，不汙偽官，使子弟間表賊事。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Lun was trapped by the rebels but did not stain himself with false office, having his sons and younger brothers secretly report rebel affairs to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Lun was trapped in rebel territory but refused false office, having his sons secretly report rebel movements to the court.

sentences.zh: 賊平，下遷晉州長史。

translations.literal: After the rebels were pacified he was demoted to Chief Administrator of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he was demoted to chief administrator of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 李齊物訟其忠，授長安令，封武邑縣男。

translations.literal: Li Qiwu pleaded his loyalty, and Lun was appointed Magistrate of Chang'an and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyi county.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiwu pleaded his loyalty, and Lun was appointed magistrate of Chang'an and enfeoffed as Baron of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，以右庶子使吐蕃，虜背約，留二歲，執倫至涇州，逼為書約城中降，倫不從，更囚邏娑城，閱六歲，終不屈，乃許還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying, as Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household he was sent to Tibet; the barbarians broke faith and detained him two years; they took Lun to Jingzhou and forced him to write urging the city to surrender; Lun refused and was moved to prison in Luosuo city for six years, never yielding, then was allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoying he was sent to Tibet as right vice director of the heir apparent's household; the Tibetans broke faith and held him two years, then took him to Jingzhou and forced him to write urging the city to surrender. Lun refused, was moved to Luosuo prison for six years, never yielded, and was finally allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 代宗見之，為感動嗚咽。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong saw him and was moved to sobbing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong saw him and was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 即具陳虜情偽、山川險易，指畫帝前，人服其詳。

translations.literal: He immediately detailed in full the barbarians' deceit and the terrain's dangers and advantages, gesturing before the emperor; people admired his thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately described Tibetan deceit and the terrain's dangers and advantages, gesturing before the emperor; all admired his thorough knowledge.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左丞，以疾改太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; because of illness he was changed to Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, then because of illness became mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈工部尚書，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one; posthumously he was made Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made minister of works, with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 衍，天寶末擢明經，調富平尉。

translations.literal: Yan, at the end of the Tianbao era passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Magistrate of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: Yan passed the Mingjing examination at the end of the Tianbao era and was assigned magistrate of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 繼母李不慈，倫自吐蕃歸，李敝衣以見，問故，曰：「衍不吾給。」

translations.literal: His stepmother Li was unkind; when Lun returned from Tibet, Li met him in ragged clothes; asked why, she said: "Yan does not provide for me.
translations.idiomatic: His stepmother Li was unkind; when Lun returned from Tibet, Li met him in ragged clothes and said Yan would not provide for her.

sentences.zh: 倫怒，召衍，將袒而鞭之，衍涕泣無所陳。

translations.literal: Lun was angry and summoned Yan to strip and whip him; Yan wept and could say nothing in his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was furious and summoned Yan to strip and whip him; Yan wept and could say nothing in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 倫弟殷趨白：「衍所稟舉送夫人所，尚何云！」

translations.literal: Lun's younger brother Yin hurried in and said: "Yan's allowance all goes to the lady's quarters — what more is there to say!
translations.idiomatic: Lun's younger brother Yin hurried in and said: "Yan's entire allowance goes to the lady's quarters — what more is there to say!

sentences.zh: 倫悟，繇是譖無入。

translations.literal: Lun understood, and from then no slander reached Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Lun understood, and from then on no slander against Yan reached him.

sentences.zh: 調清源令，勸民力田，懷附流亡，觀察使馬燧表其能，徙美原。

translations.literal: Appointed Magistrate of Qingyuan, he urged the people to farm diligently, attached fleeing population to the district, and Observation Commissioner Ma Sui memorialized his ability; he was moved to Meiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Qingyuan he urged the people to farm, won over refugees, and when observation commissioner Ma Sui memorialized his ability he was transferred to Meiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父卒，事李益謹，歲為李子郃償負不勝計，故官刺史，妻子僅免饑寒。

translations.literal: When his father died he served Li Yi carefully and for years paid Ziyi's debts beyond counting, so that though he reached the rank of prefect, his wife and children barely escaped hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he dutifully served Li Yi and for years paid off Ziyi's debts beyond counting, so that though he rose to prefect, his wife and children barely escaped hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 歷蘇、虢二州。

translations.literal: He served Suzhou and Guo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Suzhou and Guo.

sentences.zh: 虢居陜、華間，而賦數倍入，衍白太重。

translations.literal: Guo lay between Shan and Hua, yet its tax quota was several times the normal intake; Yan reported that it was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Guo lay between Shan and Hua, yet its tax quota was several times the normal intake; Yan reported that the burden was excessive.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡領度支，方聚斂，私謂衍：「前刺史無發明，公當止。」

translations.literal: Pei Yanling headed the Revenue Commission and was then amassing wealth; he privately told Yan: "Previous prefects found nothing; you should stop.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling headed the Revenue Commission and was amassing wealth; he privately told Yan: "Previous prefects found nothing to report; you should stop.

sentences.zh: 衍不聽，復奏：「州部多巖田，又郵傳劇道，屬歲無秋，民舉流亡，不蠲減租額，人無生理。

translations.literal: Yan would not listen and memorialized again: "The prefecture has much rocky field; courier routes are heavy; in years without harvest the people all fled; without reducing the tax quota there is no livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused and memorialized again: "The prefecture has much rocky land and heavy courier traffic; after years without harvest the people have fled; without reducing the tax quota they cannot survive.

sentences.zh: 臣見長吏之患，在因循不以聞。

translations.literal: The trouble I see with long-serving officials is following precedent and not reporting upward.
translations.idiomatic: The fault of long-serving officials is following precedent and failing to report upward.

sentences.zh: 不患陛下不憂恤也，患申請不實，不患朝廷不矜貸也。

translations.literal: The trouble is not that Your Majesty will not show pity — the trouble is that petitions are untrue; not that the court will not grant relief.
translations.idiomatic: The trouble is not that Your Majesty lacks compassion, but that petitions are untrue; not that the court refuses relief.

sentences.zh: 陛下拔臣大州，寧欲視民困而顧望不言哉？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty promoted me to a great prefecture — would you have me watch the people suffer and hesitate to speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty promoted me to a major prefecture — would you have me watch the people suffer in silence?"

sentences.zh: 德宗公其言，為詔度支減賦。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong praised his words and issued an edict for the Revenue Commission to reduce taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong praised his words and ordered the Revenue Commission to reduce taxes.

sentences.zh: 遷宣歙池觀察使，簡靜為百姓所懷。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Observation Commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi; his simplicity and quiet won the people's attachment.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to observation commissioner of Xuan, She, and Chi; his simplicity and restraint won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 幕府奏聘皆有名士，後多顯於時。

translations.literal: Staff memorialized for appointment were all famous gentlemen, many of whom later achieved prominence.
translations.idiomatic: His staff appointments were all distinguished men, many of whom later rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-nine and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 衍儉約畏法，室無妾媵，祿稍周於親族，葬埋嫁娶，倚以濟者數十家。

translations.literal: Yan was frugal and law-fearing, with no concubines in his household; his salary barely sufficed for his kin, yet dozens of families relied on him for burial, marriage, and other needs.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was frugal and law-abiding, kept no concubines, and though his salary barely covered his kin, dozens of families relied on him for burials and marriages.

sentences.zh: 及卒，不能蕆喪，表諸朝，賜賻帛三百段，米粟稱之。

translations.literal: At his death he could not afford burial; memorials went to court, and he was gifted three hundred bolts of silk and grain in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his family could not afford burial; memorials reached court, and the emperor granted three hundred bolts of silk and a proportionate amount of grain.

sentences.zh: 先是，天下以進奉結主恩，州藏耗竭，韋臯、劉贊、裴肅為之倡。

translations.literal: Earlier, throughout the realm tribute presentations were used to win imperial favor; prefectural treasuries were drained; Wei Gao, Liu Zan, and Pei Su had pioneered this practice.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, officials across the empire had used tribute presentations to win imperial favor, draining prefectural treasuries — a practice pioneered by Wei Gao, Liu Zan, and Pei Su.

sentences.zh: 贊死，衍代之。

translations.literal: After Zan died, Yan replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zan died, Yan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 舊貢金錫凡十八品，皆倍直市於州，民匱，多逃去，衍至，蠲革之。

translations.literal: The old tribute of eighteen kinds of gold and tin was all bought at double market price in the prefecture; the people were impoverished and many fled; when Yan arrived he abolished and reformed this.
translations.idiomatic: The old tribute of eighteen kinds of gold and tin had been purchased at double market price in each prefecture, impoverishing the people and driving many to flee; Yan abolished and reformed the practice.

sentences.zh: 居十年，嗇用度，府庫充衍。

translations.literal: In ten years he was frugal in expenditure and the treasuries were full.
translations.idiomatic: Over ten years he was frugal in spending and filled the treasuries.

sentences.zh: 及穆贊代州，以錢四十萬緡假民賦，故雖旱，人不流捐，由衍蓄積有素也。

translations.literal: When Mu Zan succeeded him in the prefecture, he loaned forty million strings to cover people's taxes; though there was drought, people did not flee or perish — because of Yan's long accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu Zan succeeded him, he was able to lend forty million strings to cover people's taxes; though drought struck, people did not flee or starve — thanks to Yan's long accumulation.

sentences.zh: 路應為觀察使，以衍有惠在民，言狀。

translations.literal: Lu Ying as observation commissioner, because Yan had shown kindness to the people, reported his merits.
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioner Lu Ying reported Yan's kindness to the people.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，詔書褒美，賜一子官云。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe an edict praised him and granted one son an office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanhe an edict praised him and granted an office to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 謚曰懿。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Yi.

sentences.zh: 盧景亮，字長晦，幽州范陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Jingliang, whose courtesy name was Changhui, was a man of Fanyang in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingliang, courtesy name Changhui, was from Fanyang in You prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤，學無不覽。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he studied everything without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he read widely in every field.

sentences.zh: 第進士、宏辭，授秘書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations and was appointed Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations and was appointed secretary.

sentences.zh: 張延賞節度荊南，表為枝江尉，掌書記。

translations.literal: Zhang Yanshang as military commissioner of Jingnan memorialized him as Magistrate of Zhijiang with charge of secretarial records.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yanshang was military commissioner of Jingnan, he recommended Jingliang as magistrate of Zhijiang with charge of secretarial records.

sentences.zh: 入遷右補闕。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital and was promoted to Right Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，景亮勸德宗曰：「陛下罪己不至，則感人不深。」

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Jingliang urged Dezong: "Unless Your Majesty's self-reproach goes far enough, you will not deeply move people.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Jingliang urged Dezong: "Unless Your Majesty's self-reproach goes deep enough, you will not move people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 景亮誌義崒然，多激發，與穆質同在諫爭地，書數上，鯁毅無所回。

translations.literal: Jingliang's will was lofty and righteous, much inspiriting; with Mu Zhi he shared remonstrance posts, submitting many memorials, unyielding and without evasion.
translations.idiomatic: Jingliang's will was lofty and righteous, and he inspired others; with Mu Zhi he held remonstrance posts, submitting many forthright memorials without yielding.

sentences.zh: 宰相李泌劾景亮等嘗眾會，漏所上語言，引善在己，即有惡歸之君。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Bi impeached Jingliang and others for once gathering in public and leaking submitted words, attributing good to themselves while assigning evil to the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Bi impeached Jingliang and others for once meeting in public and leaking submitted memorials, claiming credit for good while blaming the ruler for evil.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，貶為朗州司馬，質亦斥去，廢抑二十年。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Jingliang was demoted to Militia Commandant of Langzhou; Zhi was also expelled; they were suppressed for twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious; Jingliang was demoted to militia commandant of Langzhou and Zhi was also expelled; both were sidelined for twenty years.

sentences.zh: 至憲宗時，由和州別駕召還，再遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xianzong's time he was recalled from Vice-Prefect of Hezhou and again promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzong he was recalled from vice-prefect of Hezhou and again promoted to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 景亮善屬文，根於忠仁，有經國誌。

translations.literal: Jingliang excelled at literary composition, rooted in loyalty and benevolence, with ambition to order the state.
translations.idiomatic: Jingliang excelled at literary composition, rooted in loyalty and benevolence, with ambition to govern the state.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「人君足食足兵而又得士，天下可為也。」

translations.literal: He once said: "If the ruler has sufficient food, sufficient troops, and obtains scholars — the realm can be governed.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "If a ruler has sufficient food, sufficient troops, and wins the support of scholars, the realm can be governed.

sentences.zh: 乃興軒、頊以來至唐，剟治道之要，著書上下篇，號《三足記》。

translations.literal: Then from the time of Xuan and Zhuan through the Tang he selected the essentials of governance, compiled upper and lower volumes, and titled the work Records of the Three Sufficiencies.
translations.idiomatic: He then traced governance from the reigns of Xuan and Zhuan through the Tang, distilled its essentials, and compiled them in upper and lower volumes titled Records of the Three Sufficiencies.

sentences.zh: 又作《答問》，言免運大較及陳西戎利害，切指當世。

translations.literal: He also wrote Responses to Inquiries, discussing the broad outline of exempting transport levies and setting forth the advantages and disadvantages regarding the Western Rong, directly addressing the issues of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Responses to Inquiries, outlining proposals to reduce grain-transport burdens and analyzing the strategic costs and benefits of the Western Rong frontier, with pointed relevance to the problems of his day.

sentences.zh: 公卿伏其達古今云。

translations.literal: The grand ministers admired his mastery of past and present, it was said.
translations.idiomatic: High officials, it was said, admired his command of both antiquity and the present age.

sentences.zh: 元和初卒，贈禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Yuanhe era and was posthumously given the title of Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Yuanhe reign and was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，以直諫知名者，又有王源中，字正蒙。

translations.literal: During Xianzong's reign, among those famous for direct remonstrance, there was also Wang Yuanzhong, whose courtesy name was Zhengmeng.
translations.idiomatic: Among those famous during Emperor Xianzong's reign for forthright remonstrance, also treated here: Wang Yuanzhong, courtesy name Zhengmeng.

sentences.zh: 擢進士、宏辭，累遷左補闕。

translations.literal: He was selected as jinshi and through the Hongci examination, and was repeatedly promoted to Left Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and Hongci examinations and rose in turn to Left Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 是時，中官領禁兵，數亂法，捕臺府吏屬系軍中。

translations.literal: At that time eunuchs commanded the palace armies, repeatedly violated the law, and seized censorate and prefectural officials to hold them in the military camps.
translations.idiomatic: At that time eunuchs commanded the palace armies, repeatedly broke the law, and seized officials of the censorate and prefectural offices to detain them in the army.

sentences.zh: 源中上言：「臺憲者，紀綱地；

translations.literal: Yuanzhong submitted a memorial: "The Censorate is the ground of institutional order;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong submitted a memorial: "The censorate is where the state's institutional order is upheld;

sentences.zh: 府縣，責成之所。

translations.literal: prefectures and counties are where responsibility is enforced.
translations.idiomatic: prefectures and counties are where accountability is enforced.

sentences.zh: 設吏有罪，宜歸有司，無令北軍亂南衙，麾下重於仗內。」

translations.literal: If officials commit crimes, they should be turned over to the proper authorities; do not let the Northern Army disturb the Southern Offices, with subordinates' authority outweighing that within the staff halls."
translations.idiomatic: If officials commit crimes, they should be handed over to the proper offices. Do not let the Northern Army interfere with the Southern Offices, so that military subordinates outweigh civil authority within the palace staff."

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 累轉戶部郎中、侍郎，擢翰林學士，進承旨學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in turn to bureau director and vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, appointed Hanlin Academician, and advanced to Chief Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to bureau director and vice minister in the Ministry of Revenue, was appointed a Hanlin academician, and then promoted to chief academician.

sentences.zh: 源中嗜酒，帝召之，醉不能見。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was fond of wine; when the Emperor summoned him, he was too drunk to appear.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was fond of wine. When the Emperor summoned him, he was too drunk to attend.

sentences.zh: 及寤，憂其慢，不悔不得進也。

translations.literal: When he woke, he worried about having been disrespectful, but did not regret missing advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When he sobered up, he worried that he had been disrespectful, yet he did not regret having forfeited promotion.

sentences.zh: 他日，又如之，遂失帝意。

translations.literal: Another day he did the same again, and thus lost the Emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he did the same again, and so lost the Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 以疾自言，出為山南西道節度使，入拜刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He cited illness on his own initiative, was sent out as military governor of Shannan West Circuit, and on return was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to leave on grounds of illness, was sent out as military governor of Shannan West Circuit, and on returning to court was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 未幾，領天平節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he also held the post of military governor of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also served as military governor of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 開成三年卒，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Kaicheng and was posthumously given the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Kaicheng and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 源中淡名利，率身治人，約而簡，當時咨美。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was indifferent to fame and profit, led by example in governing people, concise and simple; contemporaries praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong cared little for fame or profit, governed people by personal example in a spare and straightforward way, and won wide praise in his day.

sentences.zh: 薛蘋，河中寶鼎人。

translations.literal: Xue Ping was a man of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ping, a native of Baoding in Hezhong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七世祖道實，為隋禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Daoshi served as Minister of Rites under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor Daoshi had served as Minister of Rites under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 父順為奉天尉，與楊國忠有舊，及用事，將引之，輒謝絕。

translations.literal: His father Shun was magistrate of Fengtian; he had old ties with Yang Guozhong, and when Yang came to power and meant to recommend him, he repeatedly declined.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shun was magistrate of Fengtian. He had old ties with Yang Guozhong, but when Yang came to power and tried to recommend him, he repeatedly refused.

sentences.zh: 蘋以吏最拜長安令，歷虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Ping, through top administrative rating, was appointed magistrate of Chang'an and served as prefect of Guo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, rated highest in administrative performance, was appointed magistrate of Chang'an and later served as prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，奏最，擢湖南觀察使，徙浙東，以治行遷浙西，加御史大夫，累封河東郡公。

translations.literal: During Xianzong's reign, through highest performance report, he was promoted to Hu'nan surveillance commissioner, transferred to Zhedong, moved to Zhexi for his administrative record, was given the additional title of Censor-in-Chief, and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianzong's reign he received the highest performance rating, was promoted to Hu'nan surveillance commissioner, transferred to Zhedong, and then moved to Zhexi for his record of governance. He was given the additional title of Censor-in-Chief and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 所居守法度，務在安人。

translations.literal: Wherever he served, he upheld law and regulation, striving to bring peace to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he upheld law and regulation and devoted himself to keeping the people secure.

sentences.zh: 治身觳薄，所衣綠袍更十年，至緋衣乃易。

translations.literal: He governed himself with frugal simplicity; the green robe he wore was mended for ten years, and he only replaced it when promoted to the crimson robe.
translations.idiomatic: He lived with austere frugality, mending the same green robe for ten years and replacing it only when promoted to the crimson robe of higher rank.

sentences.zh: 居三鎮，聲樂不聞於家，所得祿，即分散親屬故人，而無余藏。

translations.literal: During three terms as regional governor, no music was heard in his household; his salary was immediately distributed to relatives and old friends, and he kept no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Over three terms as regional governor, no music was heard in his home. He distributed his salary at once among relatives and old friends and kept nothing in reserve.

sentences.zh: 除左散騎常侍，年七十致仕。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Regular Cavalry Attendant, and at seventy he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Regular Cavalry Attendant and retired from office at seventy.

sentences.zh: 是時有年過蘋不肯去，故論者高蘋。

translations.literal: At that time there were those past retirement age who would not leave office, so commentators esteemed Ping highly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many men past retirement age still refused to leave office, so commentators held Ping in especially high regard.

sentences.zh: 居四年，卒，贈工部尚書，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: After four years at home, he died; he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Four years after retiring, he died. He was posthumously appointed Minister of Works and given the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 蘋於文章中長於詩。

translations.literal: Among literary compositions Ping excelled especially at poetry.
