translations.idiomatic: Among his literary works, Ping excelled above all at poetry.

sentences.zh: 蘋兄 芳兄芳，有器幹。

translations.literal: Ping's brother Fang — Brother Fang was capable and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's brother Fang was a man of ability and force of character.

sentences.zh: 萊與莘，其母代宗從母也。

translations.literal: Lai and Shen — their mother was a cousin of Emperor Daizong's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lai and Shen—their mother was a cousin of Emperor Daizong's mother.

sentences.zh: 以外戚奉朝請，皆贊善大夫。

translations.literal: As maternal relatives they attended court and all held the title of Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial affines they attended court and all held the rank of mentor.

sentences.zh: 莘子 膺莘子膺，大和初，為右補闕內供奉。

translations.literal: Shen's son Ying — Shen's son Ying, at the beginning of Dahe, served as Right Remonstrance Censor on internal palace duty.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's son Ying, at the beginning of the Dahe era, served as Right Remonstrance Censor on internal palace duty.

sentences.zh: 其弟齊，佐興元李絳幕府，絳遇害，齊死於難。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qi assisted Li Jiang's staff at Xingyuan; when Jiang was killed, Qi died in the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Qi served on Li Jiang's staff at Xingyuan. When Jiang was murdered, Qi died in the same calamity.

sentences.zh: 膺聞，不及請，馳赴之，哀甚，聞者垂泣。

translations.literal: When Ying heard, without waiting for permission he galloped there; his grief was profound, and those who heard of it wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying heard the news, he set out at once without waiting for leave. His grief was overwhelming, and those who witnessed it wept.

sentences.zh: 後歷工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Later he served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 衞次公，字從周，河中河東人。

translations.literal: Wei Cigong, whose courtesy name was Congzhou, was a man of Hedong in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cigong, courtesy name Congzhou, was from Hedong in Hezhong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，禮部侍郎潘炎異之，曰：「國器也。」

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; Vice Minister of Rites Pan Yan was impressed and said: "He is a pillar of the state."
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination. Vice Minister of Rites Pan Yan was impressed and said, "He is a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 高其第。

translations.literal: He was placed at the top rank.
translations.idiomatic: Pan placed him at the top of the examination list.

sentences.zh: 調渭南尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as aide to the magistrate of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as aide to the magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 嚴震在興元，辟佐其府。

translations.literal: When Yan Zhen was at Xingyuan, he recruited him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhen was stationed at Xingyuan, he recruited Cigong to his staff.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，擢左補闕、翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Censor and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyuan era he was promoted to Left Remonstrance Censor and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 德宗崩，與鄭絪皆召至金鑾殿。

translations.literal: When Dezong died, he and Zheng Yin were both summoned to the Golden Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong died, he and Zheng Yin were both summoned to the Golden Hall.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子久疾，禁中或傳更議所立，眾失色。

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince had long been ill, and inside the palace there were rumors of debating who should succeed; everyone turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince had long been ill, and inside the palace there were rumors that the succession was being reconsidered. Everyone turned pale.

sentences.zh: 次公曰：「太子雖久疾，冢嫡也，內外系心久矣。

translations.literal: Cigong said: "Though the crown prince has long been ill, he is the eldest legitimate son; within and without, hearts have long been bound to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong said, "Though the crown prince has long been ill, he is the eldest legitimate son. Within the palace and without, all hearts have long been bound to him.

sentences.zh: 必不得已，宜立廣陵王。」

translations.literal: If it absolutely cannot be helped, the Prince of Guangling should be installed."
translations.idiomatic: If there is truly no alternative, the Prince of Guangling should be enthroned.

sentences.zh: 絪隨贊之，議乃定。

translations.literal: Yin immediately endorsed this, and the deliberation was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yin immediately endorsed this, and the succession question was settled.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，王叔文等用事，輕弄威柄，次公與絪多所持正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, Wang Shuwen and others held power and lightly wielded authority; Cigong and Yin often upheld what was right.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, Wang Shuwen and his faction held power and wielded authority lightly. Cigong and Yin often held firm to what was right.

sentences.zh: 知禮部貢舉，斥華取實，不為權力侵橈。

translations.literal: As head of the Ministry of Rites examinations, he rejected ornament and selected substance, without letting power twist the process.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the Ministry of Rites examinations, he rejected showy talent in favor of genuine ability and would not let power distort the selection process.

sentences.zh: 由中書舍人充史館修撰，改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: From Secretariat Drafter he served as historiography compiler and was changed to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: From his post as Secretariat drafter he served as historiography compiler and was then transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 絪以宰相罷，坐與善，下除太子賓客。

translations.literal: Yin was removed as chancellor; Cigong was implicated for association with him and demoted to Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin was dismissed as chancellor, Cigong was punished for association with him and demoted to mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 久乃為陜、虢州觀察使，蠲橫租錢歲三百萬。

translations.literal: After a long while he became surveillance commissioner of Shan and Guo prefectures, remitting three million in improper levies per year.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he became surveillance commissioner of Shan and Guo prefectures and remitted three million cash in improper levies each year.

sentences.zh: 復入為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 故英公李勣、大理卿徐有功之孫，皆以負不得調，次公召見曰：「子之祖，勛在王府，寧限常格乎？」

translations.literal: The grandsons of the late Duke of Ying, Li Ji, and of Senior Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Yougong, both could not receive appointment due to debts; Cigong summoned them and said: "Your grandfathers' merit served the imperial house — should ordinary rules limit you?"
translations.idiomatic: The grandsons of the late Duke of Ying, Li Ji, and of Senior Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Yougong could not receive appointments because of debts. Cigong summoned them and said, "Your grandfathers' merit served the imperial house. Should ordinary rules limit you?

sentences.zh: 即優補而遣。

translations.literal: He immediately gave them preferential appointments and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately gave them preferential appointments and sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 進尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時方討蔡，數建請罷兵，帝將相之，制稿具而蔡捷書至，乃追止。

translations.literal: At the time the court was campaigning against Cai; he repeatedly urged halting the troops. The Emperor was about to make him chancellor, the draft edict was ready, but when news of victory over Cai arrived, the appointment was recalled and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was campaigning against Cai, and he repeatedly urged that the troops be withdrawn. The Emperor was about to appoint him chancellor and the draft edict was ready, but when news of victory over Cai arrived the appointment was recalled.

sentences.zh: 以檢校工部尚書為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: He was made military governor of Huai'nan with the acting title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of Huainan with the acting title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 久之，召還，道病卒，年六十六，贈太子少傅，謚曰敬。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled; he died of illness on the road, age sixty-six; he was posthumously given Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled, but died of illness on the road at sixty-six. He was posthumously appointed Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 次公本善琴，方未顯時，京兆尹李齊運使子與遊，請授之法，次公拒絕，因終身不復鼓。

translations.literal: Cigong was originally skilled at the zither; before he had risen to prominence, Metropolitan Governor Li Qiyun had his son associate with him and asked to be taught the method; Cigong refused, and thereafter never played again in his life.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong was originally skilled at the zither. Before he had risen to prominence, Metropolitan Governor Li Qiyun had his son associate with him and asked to be taught the art. Cigong refused, and from then on never played again for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 其節尚終始完絜。

translations.literal: His integrity prized consistency from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity was marked by consistency and purity from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 次公子 洙子洙，舉進士，尚臨真公主，檢校秘書少監、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Cigong's son Zhu — Son Zhu passed the jinshi, married Princess Linzhen, and held acting Junior Director of the Secretariat and Commander of the Imperial Son-in-law's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Cigong's son Zhu passed the jinshi, married Princess Linzhen, and served as acting junior director of the Secretariat and commander of the imperial son-in-law's guard.

sentences.zh: 文宗曰：「洙起名家，以文進，宜諫官寵之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong said: "Zhu comes from a distinguished family and rose through literature; he should be favored with a remonstrance post."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong said, "Zhu comes from a distinguished family and rose through literary talent. He should be favored with a remonstrance post.

sentences.zh: 乃為左拾遺，歷義成節度使。

translations.literal: He was made Left Reminder and later served as military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Reminder and later served as military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 咸通中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Xiantong era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Xiantong reign.

sentences.zh: 薛戎，字元夫，河中寶鼎人。

translations.literal: Xue Rong, whose courtesy name was Yuanfu, was a man of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Rong, courtesy name Yuanfu, was from Baoding in Hezhong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 客毗陵陽羨山，年四十餘不仕。

translations.literal: He lived as a guest on Mount Yangxian in Piling, and past forty still did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He lived as a guest on Mount Yangxian in Piling and, past forty, still refused to take office.

sentences.zh: 江西觀察使李衡辟署幕府，三返乃肯應。

translations.literal: Jiangxi surveillance commissioner Li Heng recruited him to his staff; only after three refusals did he agree.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi surveillance commissioner Li Heng recruited him to his staff, but only after three refusals did he agree to serve.

sentences.zh: 故宰相齊映代衡，奏留之。

translations.literal: Former chancellor Qi Ying replaced Heng and memorialized to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Former chancellor Qi Ying replaced Heng and memorialized to retain him on staff.

sentences.zh: 府罷，復歸陽羨。

translations.literal: When the staff was dissolved, he returned again to Yangxian.
translations.idiomatic: When the staff was dissolved, he returned once more to Yangxian.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使柳冕辟佐其府。

translations.literal: Fujian surveillance commissioner Liu Mian recruited him as staff aide.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian surveillance commissioner Liu Mian recruited him as a staff aide.

sentences.zh: 先是，馬總佐鄭滑府，監軍宦人誣劾之，貶泉州別駕。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ma Zong had served on the Zheng-Slip circuit staff; the supervising military eunuch falsely impeached him and had him demoted to assistant prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ma Zong had served on the Zheng-Slip circuit staff. The supervising military eunuch falsely impeached him and had him demoted to assistant prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 冕欲除總以附幸家，即使戎攝刺史，按置其罪。

translations.literal: Mian wished to remove Zong to please the favored faction, and had Rong act as prefect to investigate and establish his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Mian wished to remove Zong to please the favored faction and had Rong act as prefect to investigate and establish charges against him.

sentences.zh: 戎曰：「以是待我耶？

translations.literal: Rong said: "Is this how you treat me?
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Is this how you treat me?

sentences.zh: 我始不願仕，正謂此爾！」

translations.literal: I first refused office precisely because of this sort of thing!"
translations.idiomatic: I refused office in the first place precisely because of this sort of thing!

sentences.zh: 不肯從，還白其狀。

translations.literal: He refused to comply and returned to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to comply and returned to report what had happened.

sentences.zh: 冕怒，據案引戎入，戎叱引者曰：「見賓客乃爾乎？」

translations.literal: Mian grew angry; leaning on his desk he had men drag Rong in; Rong shouted at those dragging him: "Is this how you receive a guest?"
translations.idiomatic: Mian grew angry. Leaning on his desk, he had men drag Rong in. Rong shouted at the men pulling him, "Is this how you receive a guest?

sentences.zh: 由東廂進。

translations.literal: He entered through the east wing.
translations.idiomatic: He entered through the east wing instead.

sentences.zh: 冕度未可屈，揖而去，囚之它館，環兵脅辱之，累月，戎終不為屈。

translations.literal: Seeing he could not be bent, Mian bowed and let him leave; then imprisoned him in another lodge, surrounded him with soldiers to threaten and humiliate him — for months — yet Rong never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Rong could not be broken, Mian bowed and let him leave, then imprisoned him in another lodge and surrounded him with soldiers to threaten and humiliate him. For months Rong never yielded.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使杜佑聞之，書責冕，會冕亦病死，得解，自放江湖間。

translations.literal: Huainan military governor Du You heard of this and wrote reproaching Mian; as Mian also died of illness, Rong was released and let himself roam the rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan military governor Du You heard of this and wrote to reproach Mian. Mian also happened to die of illness, and Rong was released to roam freely among the rivers and lakes.

sentences.zh: 復為藩府交奏，稍遷河南令。

translations.literal: Regional staffs again submitted him in turn; he was gradually promoted to magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Regional staffs again recommended him in turn, and he was gradually promoted to magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀討鎮州，所過吏迎廷畏不及，治道前驅，惟戎境內按故無所治迓。

translations.literal: Tuhutuo Chenghui's campaign against Zhenzhou — wherever he passed, officials received him with fear they could not match, repairing roads and riding ahead as escort; only within Rong's jurisdiction did he proceed as usual with nothing arranged for welcome.
translations.idiomatic: On Tuhutuo Chenghui's campaign against Zhenzhou, officials everywhere received him with fearful haste, repairing roads and riding ahead as escort. Only within Rong's jurisdiction did Chenghui proceed as usual, with nothing prepared to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 留府卒犯令者，縛置獄，留守怒，遣將略出之，不與。

translations.literal: Garrison soldiers who violated orders were bound and put in prison; the acting governor was angry and sent a general to seize them by force; Rong would not yield them.
translations.idiomatic: When garrison soldiers violated orders, Rong bound them and placed them in prison. The acting governor was angry and sent a general to seize them by force, but Rong would not release them.

sentences.zh: 累遷浙東觀察使，所部州觸酒禁者罪當死，橘未貢先鬻者死，戎弛其禁。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Zhedong surveillance commissioner; in his jurisdiction, violating the wine prohibition was punishable by death, and selling oranges before tribute was due was also death; Rong relaxed these prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Zhedong surveillance commissioner. In his jurisdiction, violating the wine prohibition or selling oranges before tribute was due was punishable by death, and Rong relaxed both prohibitions.

sentences.zh: 卒治下，年七十五，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died in office at seventy-five; he was posthumously given Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at seventy-five and was posthumously appointed Left Regular Cavalry Attendant.

sentences.zh: 戎為吏，不尚約束詭名譽，其有善，歸之所部。

translations.literal: As an official Rong did not pursue constrained showy reputation; whatever good there was, he attributed to his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: As an official, Rong did not cultivate a showy reputation through contrived restraint. Whatever good was achieved, he credited to the region he governed.

sentences.zh: 故居官時無灼灼可驚者，已罷則懷之。

translations.literal: Thus while in office there was nothing dazzlingly remarkable, but after he left people cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: Thus while he held office there was nothing dazzlingly remarkable about him, yet after he left people cherished his memory.

sentences.zh: 悉奉稟赒濟內外親，無疏遠皆歸之。

translations.literal: He devoted all income to support and relieve inner and outer kin; none were excluded, all came to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted all his income to supporting and relieving relatives near and far. None were excluded; all came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 既病，以所有分遺之曰：「吾死矣，可持為歸資！」

translations.literal: When ill, he divided all he possessed among them, saying: "I am dying — take this as funds for your journey home!"
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, he divided all he possessed among them, saying, "I am dying. Take this as funds for your journey home!

sentences.zh: 眾皆哭而去。

translations.literal: All wept as they departed.
translations.idiomatic: All wept as they departed.

sentences.zh: 戎弟 放弟放，端厚寡言。

translations.literal: Rong's brother Fang — Brother Fang was steady, generous, and sparing of words.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's brother Fang was upright, generous, and sparing of words.

sentences.zh: 第進士，擢累兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and was promoted repeatedly to bureau director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and rose in turn to bureau director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 穆宗為太子，拜侍讀，及即位，參贊機命。

translations.literal: When Muzong was heir apparent, Fang was appointed study companion; when Muzong took the throne, he participated in deliberating imperial decisions.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong was heir apparent, Fang was appointed his study companion. When Muzong took the throne, Fang helped deliberate imperial decisions.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「小子新立，懼不克荷，先生宜相，以輔不逮。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to him: "I have just ascended the throne as a young man and fear I cannot bear the burden — Sir, you ought to serve as chancellor to assist where I fall short.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to him, "I have just ascended the throne as a young man and fear I cannot bear the burden. Sir, you ought to serve as chancellor and assist where I fall short.

sentences.zh: 放叩頭曰：「臣庸淺，不足塵大任，自有賢能處之。」

translations.literal: Fang kowtowed and said: "Your servant is shallow and mediocre, unworthy to sully so great a post — there are able men who should handle it."
translations.idiomatic: Fang kowtowed and said, "Your servant is shallow and mediocre, unworthy to sully so great a post. There are able men who should handle it.

sentences.zh: 帝美其誠，進工部侍郎、集賢學士，寵待尤至。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his sincerity, promoted him to Vice Minister of Works and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and favored him exceptionally.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his sincerity, promoted him to Vice Minister of Works and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and favored him with exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 改刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問：「朕欲學經與史，何先？」

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked: "I wish to study the classics and history — which should come first?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once asked, "I wish to study the classics and history. Which should come first?

sentences.zh: 放曰：「《六經》者，聖人之言，孔子所發明，天人之極也。

translations.literal: Fang replied: "The Six Classics are the words of the sages, elucidated by Confucius — the ultimate standard of Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: Fang replied, "The Six Classics are the words of the sages, elucidated by Confucius. They are the ultimate standard of Heaven and man.

sentences.zh: 《史記》道成敗得失，亦足以鑒，然謬於是非，非《六經》比。」

translations.literal: The Records of the Grand Historian recounts success and failure, gain and loss, and is also sufficient as a mirror — yet it errs in right and wrong and cannot compare with the Six Classics."
translations.idiomatic: The Records of the Grand Historian recounts success and failure, gain and loss, and can serve as a mirror as well, yet it errs in matters of right and wrong and cannot compare with the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吾聞學者白首不能通一經，安得其要乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I have heard that scholars grow white-haired without mastering even one classic — how then can one grasp their essentials?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I have heard that scholars grow white-haired without mastering even one classic. How then can one grasp their essentials?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「《論語》，《六經》之菁華也；

translations.literal: He answered: "The Analects is the finest essence of the Six Classics;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Analects is the finest essence of the Six Classics;

sentences.zh: 《孝經》，人倫之本也。

translations.literal: the Classic of Filial Piety is the root of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: and the Classic of Filial Piety is the root of human relations.

sentences.zh: 漢時《論語》首立於學官。

translations.literal: In Han times the Analects was first established in the official schools.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the Analects was first established in the official schools.

sentences.zh: 光武令虎賁士皆習《孝經》，玄宗為註訓，蓋人知孝慈，則氣感和樂也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu ordered the tiger guards all to study the Classic of Filial Piety, and Emperor Xuanzong provided commentary and instruction — for when people know filial piety and compassion, the vital forces harmonize and joy prevails."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu ordered the tiger guards all to study the Classic of Filial Piety, and Emperor Xuanzong provided commentary and instruction, for when people know filial piety and compassion, the vital forces harmonize and joy prevails.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「聖人以孝為至德要道，信然。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The sages take filial piety as the highest virtue and essential way — truly so."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The sages take filial piety as the highest virtue and essential way. Truly so.

sentences.zh: 終江西觀察使，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: He ended as Jiangxi observation commissioner, and his posthumous title was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Jiangxi observation commissioner, and his posthumous title was Jian.

sentences.zh: 胡證，字啟中，河中河東人。

translations.literal: Hu Zheng, whose courtesy name was Qizhong, was a man of Hedong in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zheng, courtesy name Qizhong, was a native of Hedong in Hezhong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第，渾瑊美其才，又以鄉府奏寘幕下。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination. Hun Zhen praised his talent, and the provincial authorities also recommended him and placed him on Hun's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination. Hun Zhen praised his talent, and the provincial authorities also recommended him and placed him on Hun's staff.

sentences.zh: 繇殿中侍御史為韶州刺史，以母老辭，為太子舍人。

translations.literal: From Attendant Censor of the Palace he became prefect of Shaozhou; citing his mother's age, he declined and was made Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: From Attendant Censor of the Palace he became prefect of Shaozhou, but citing his mother's age he declined and was made Gentleman Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 更從襄陽於頔，署掌書記。

translations.literal: He then followed Yu Di at Xiangyang and was appointed chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Yu Di at Xiangyang and was appointed chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 田弘正以魏博內屬，請使自副，詔兼御史中丞，為弘正副使。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng brought Weibo back under the court, he requested an envoy as his deputy; the court ordered Hu to serve concurrently as Vice Censor-in-Chief and as Tian's deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng brought Weibo back under the court, he requested an envoy as his deputy. The court ordered Hu to serve concurrently as Vice Censor-in-Chief and as Tian's deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On entering the capital he was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the capital he was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 元和九年，党項屢擾邊，而單於都護府累更武將，職事廢，證以儒而勇選拜振武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe the Tangut repeatedly harassed the frontier, while the Chanyu Protectorate had repeatedly changed military commanders and its duties had fallen into disuse. Hu, selected for being a scholar yet brave, was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanhe the Tangut repeatedly harassed the frontier, while the Chanyu Protectorate had repeatedly changed military commanders and its duties had fallen into disuse. Hu, selected for being a scholar yet brave, was appointed military commissioner of Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 道河中，時趙宗儒為帥，以州民入謁，裏人榮之。

translations.literal: Passing through Hezhong, where Zhao Zongru was commander, the people of the prefecture came to pay their respects; his neighbors took pride in it.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Hezhong, where Zhao Zongru was commander, the people of the prefecture came to pay their respects, and his neighbors took pride in it.

sentences.zh: 居四年，召任金吾大將軍，又充京西、京北巡邊使。

translations.literal: After four years he was summoned to serve as General of the Golden Guard and also appointed frontier inspector of the western and northern capital circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was summoned to serve as General of the Golden Guard and also appointed frontier inspector of the western and northern capital circuits.

sentences.zh: 太和公主降回鶻，以檢校工部尚書為和親使。

translations.literal: When Princess Taihe was sent in marriage to the Uyghurs, he was made Acting Minister of Works and commissioner for the marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Taihe was sent in marriage to the Uyghurs, he was made Acting Minister of Works and commissioner for the marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 舊制，行人有私覿禮，縣官不能具，召富人子納資於使而命之官。

translations.literal: By old custom envoys received private presentation gifts, which the county officials could not supply; sons of wealthy families were summoned to pay funds to the envoy and were given offices in return.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom envoys received private presentation gifts, which the county officials could not supply. Sons of wealthy families were summoned to pay funds to the envoy and were given offices in return.

sentences.zh: 證請儉受省費，以絕鬻官之濫。

translations.literal: Hu requested to accept gifts frugally and reduce expenses, so as to end the abuse of selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: Hu requested to accept gifts frugally and reduce expenses, so as to end the abuse of selling offices.

sentences.zh: 次漠南，虜人欲屈脅之，且言使者必易胡服，又欲主便道疾驅者，證固不從，以唐官儀自將，訖不辱命。

translations.literal: When they reached south of the desert, the barbarians wished to humiliate and coerce him, saying the envoy must change into barbarian dress and insisting he take a shortcut at full speed. Hu steadfastly refused, conducting himself by Tang official protocol, and in the end did not disgrace his mission.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached south of the desert, the barbarians wished to humiliate and coerce him, saying the envoy must change into barbarian dress and insisting he take a shortcut at full speed. Hu steadfastly refused, conducting himself by Tang official protocol, and in the end did not disgrace his mission.

sentences.zh: 還，拜工部侍郎，改京兆尹、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Works, then transferred to Intendant of Jingzhao and Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Vice Minister of Works, then transferred to Intendant of Jingzhao and Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，以戶部尚書判度支，固辭，拜嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli he was ordered to serve as Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of the treasury; he firmly declined and was appointed military commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Baoli he was ordered to serve as Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of the treasury. He firmly declined and was appointed military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-one and was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one and was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 廣有舶貝奇寶，證厚殖財自奉，養奴數百人，營第脩行裏，彌亙閭陌，車服器用珍侈，遂號京師高訾。

translations.literal: Guangzhou had abundant imported shells and rare treasures. Hu amassed great wealth for his own comfort, kept several hundred slaves, and built mansions in Xiuhang Ward stretching across lanes and streets. His carriages, robes, and utensils were all rare and extravagant, and he came to be known in the capital for his towering reputation for wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou had abundant imported shells and rare treasures. Hu amassed great wealth for his own comfort, kept several hundred slaves, and built mansions in Xiuhang Ward stretching across lanes and streets. His carriages, robes, and utensils were all rare and extravagant, and he came to be known in the capital for his towering reputation for wealth.

sentences.zh: 素與賈餗善。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Jia Su.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been on good terms with Jia Su.

sentences.zh: 李訓敗，衛軍利其財，聲言餗匿其家，爭入剽劫，執其子溵內左軍，至斬以徇。

translations.literal: When Li Xun was defeated, the imperial guard coveted Hu's wealth, claiming that Jia Su was hiding at his house. They rushed in to plunder and loot, seized his son Yin and held him in the Left Army, and finally executed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xun was defeated, the imperial guard coveted Hu's wealth, claiming that Jia Su was hiding at his house. They rushed in to plunder and loot, seized his son Yin and held him in the Left Army, and finally executed him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 證旅力絕人。

translations.literal: Hu's physical strength was unmatched among men.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's physical strength was unmatched among men.

sentences.zh: 晉公裴度未顯時，羸服私飲，為武士所窘。

translations.literal: When Duke of Jin Pei Du had not yet risen to prominence, he went out in shabby clothes to drink in private and was harassed by bravos.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Jin Pei Du had not yet risen to prominence, he went out in shabby clothes to drink in private and was harassed by bravos.

sentences.zh: 證聞，突入坐客上，引觥三釂，客皆失色。

translations.literal: When Hu heard of it he burst in and sat above the guests, draining three cups in succession; the guests all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu heard of it he burst in and sat above the guests, draining three cups in succession. The guests all turned pale.

sentences.zh: 因取鐵燈檠，摘枝葉，擽合其跗，橫膝上，謂客曰：「我欲為酒令，飲不釂者，以此擊之！」

translations.literal: He then took an iron lamp stand, stripped off its branches and leaves, twisted its base together, laid it across his knee, and said to the guests: "I wish to make a drinking rule — whoever does not drain his cup, I shall strike with this!"
translations.idiomatic: He then took an iron lamp stand, stripped off its branches and leaves, twisted its base together, laid it across his knee, and said to the guests, "I wish to make a drinking rule. Whoever does not drain his cup, I shall strike with this!

sentences.zh: 眾唯唯。

translations.literal: The crowd assented in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd assented in fear.

sentences.zh: 證一飲輒數升，次授客，客流離盤杓不能盡，證欲擊之，諸惡少叩頭請去，證悉驅出。

translations.literal: Hu drank several sheng at a single draught, then passed the cup to the guests. The guests fumbled with the dishes and ladles and could not finish; when Hu was about to strike them, the young ruffians kowtowed and begged to leave, and he drove them all out.
translations.idiomatic: Hu drank several sheng at a single draught, then passed the cup to the guests. The guests fumbled with the dishes and ladles and could not finish. When Hu was about to strike them, the young ruffians kowtowed and begged to leave, and he drove them all out.

sentences.zh: 故時人稱其俠。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time called him chivalrous.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore people of the time called him chivalrous.

sentences.zh: 丁公著，字平子，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Ding Gongzhu, whose courtesy name was Pingzi, was a man of Wu in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gongzhu, courtesy name Pingzi, was a native of Wu in Suzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三歲喪母。

translations.literal: He lost his mother at the age of three.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 甫七歲，見鄰媼抱子，哀感不肯食，請於父緒，願絕粒學老子道，父聽之。

translations.literal: At just seven he saw a neighboring old woman holding her child, was moved to grief, and refused to eat. He asked his father Xu to let him abstain from food and study the Way of Laozi, and his father consented.
translations.idiomatic: At just seven he saw a neighboring old woman holding her child, was moved to grief, and refused to eat. He asked his father Xu to let him abstain from food and study the Way of Laozi, and his father consented.

sentences.zh: 稍長，父勉敕就學。

translations.literal: When he grew older his father urged and admonished him to pursue formal study.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew older his father urged and admonished him to pursue formal study.

sentences.zh: 舉明經高第，授集賢校書郎，不滿秩輒去，侍養於家。

translations.literal: He passed the mingjing examination at the top tier and was appointed Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, but before completing his term he left to serve and care for his parents at home.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the mingjing examination at the top tier and was appointed Collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, but before completing his term he left to serve and care for his parents at home.

sentences.zh: 父喪，負土作冢，貌力臒惙，見者憂其死孝。

translations.literal: When his father died he carried earth to build the tomb himself. His appearance grew gaunt and his strength wasted away; those who saw him feared he would die from excessive filial mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he carried earth to build the tomb himself. His appearance grew gaunt and his strength wasted away, and those who saw him feared he would die from excessive filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 觀察使薛蘋表上至行，詔刺史吊問，賜粟帛，旌闕其閭。

translations.literal: Observation commissioner Xue Pin memorialized his supreme conduct. The court ordered the prefect to offer condolences, granted grain and cloth, and erected a memorial gate at his lane.
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioner Xue Pin memorialized his supreme conduct. The court ordered the prefect to offer condolences, granted grain and cloth, and erected a memorial gate at his lane.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使李吉甫表授太子文學，兼集賢校理。

translations.literal: Huainan military commissioner Li Jifu memorialized to appoint him Erudite of the Heir Apparent and concurrent collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan military commissioner Li Jifu memorialized to appoint him Erudite of the Heir Apparent and concurrent collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 會入輔政，擢為右補闕，遷直學士，充皇太子、諸王侍讀，因著《太子諸王訓》十篇。

translations.literal: When Li entered the capital to assist in governance, Ding was promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor, transferred to Direct Academician, and appointed study companion to the heir apparent and the princes. He thereupon composed ten chapters of Admonitions for the Heir Apparent and the Princes.
translations.idiomatic: When Li entered the capital to assist in governance, Ding was promoted to Right Remonstrance Censor, transferred to Direct Academician, and appointed study companion to the heir apparent and the princes. He thereupon composed ten chapters of Admonitions for the Heir Apparent and the Princes.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，未聽政，召居禁中，條詢治理，且許以相。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended the throne and had not yet taken up governance, he summoned Ding to reside within the inner palace, questioned him item by item on administration, and even promised him the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended the throne and had not yet taken up governance, he summoned Ding to reside within the inner palace, questioned him item by item on administration, and even promised him the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 公著陳讓牢切，乃擢給事中，遷工部侍郎，知吏部選事。

translations.literal: Gongzhu declined with earnest and forceful remonstrance, whereupon he was promoted to Supervising Censor, transferred to Vice Minister of Works, and given charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu declined with earnest and forceful remonstrance, whereupon he was promoted to Supervising Censor, transferred to Vice Minister of Works, and given charge of personnel selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 公著內知帝欲進用，故辭疾求外，遷授浙西觀察使，徙為河南尹，治以清靜聞。

translations.literal: Gongzhu inwardly knew the Emperor wished to advance him further, so he pleaded illness and sought an outside post. He was transferred and appointed Zhexi observation commissioner, then moved to Intendant of Henan, and became known for governing with clarity and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu inwardly knew the Emperor wished to advance him further, so he pleaded illness and sought an outside post. He was transferred and appointed Zhexi observation commissioner, then moved to Intendant of Henan, and became known for governing with clarity and restraint.

sentences.zh: 四遷禮部尚書、翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: After four promotions he became Minister of Rites and Lecturing Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions he became Minister of Rites and Lecturing Academician of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 長慶中，浙東災癘，拜觀察使，詔賜米七萬斛，使賑饑捐。

translations.literal: During Changqing, when Zhedong suffered epidemic disaster, he was appointed observation commissioner. The court granted seventy thousand hu of grain and ordered him to relieve famine and levy donations.
translations.idiomatic: During Changqing, when Zhedong suffered epidemic disaster, he was appointed observation commissioner. The court granted seventy thousand hu of grain and ordered him to relieve famine and levy donations.

sentences.zh: 久之，入為太常卿。

translations.literal: After some time he entered the capital as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he entered the capital as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 太和中，以病丐身還鄉里，卒，年六十四，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In Taihe he pleaded illness and requested to return to his home district. He died at the age of sixty-four and was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he pleaded illness and requested to return to his home district. He died at the age of sixty-four and was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 公著清約守道，每進一官，輒憂見顏間。

translations.literal: Gongzhu was frugal and steadfast in the Way; with every promotion he showed worry upon his face.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu was frugal and steadfast in the Way. With every promotion he showed worry upon his face.

sentences.zh: 四十喪妻，終身不畜妾。

translations.literal: He lost his wife at forty and never kept a concubine for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his wife at forty and never kept a concubine for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 及卒，天下惜之。

translations.literal: When he died the whole realm mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the whole realm mourned him.

sentences.zh: 崔弘禮，字從周，系出博陵，北齊左僕射懷遠六世孫。

translations.literal: Cui Hongli, whose courtesy name was Congzhou, was descended from Boling and was a sixth-generation descendant of Huaiyuan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs under Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hongli, courtesy name Congzhou, was descended from Boling and was a sixth-generation descendant of Huaiyuan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 磊磊有大誌，通兵略。

translations.literal: He was open and forthright with great ambition and understood military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was open and forthright with great ambition and understood military strategy.

sentences.zh: 過宣武，從劉玄佐獵夷門，玄佐酒酣，顧曰：「崔生獨不知此樂邪？」

translations.literal: Passing through Xuanwu he joined Liu Xuanzuo in hunting at Yimen Gate. When Liu was deep in wine he turned and said: "Does young Cui alone not know this pleasure?"
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Xuanwu he joined Liu Xuanzuo in hunting at Yimen Gate. When Liu was deep in wine he turned and said, "Does young Cui alone not know this pleasure?

sentences.zh: 弘禮笑曰：「我固喜武，請為公歡。」

translations.literal: Hongli smiled and said: "I have always loved martial affairs — allow me to join your revelry."
translations.idiomatic: Hongli smiled and said, "I have always loved martial affairs. Allow me to join your revelry.

sentences.zh: 玄佐臂鷹與弘禮馳逐，急緩在手，一軍驚曰：「安得此奇客？」

translations.literal: Liu took a hawk on his arm and raced with Hongli in pursuit; controlling pace and speed in his hands, the whole army exclaimed in astonishment: "Where did such an extraordinary guest come from?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu took a hawk on his arm and raced with Hongli in pursuit, controlling pace and speed in his hands. The whole army exclaimed in astonishment, "Where did such an extraordinary guest come from?

sentences.zh: 玄佐大悅，欲留之，固辭，厚為資餉。

translations.literal: Liu was greatly pleased and wished to keep him, but Hongli firmly declined and was richly supplied with gifts and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Liu was greatly pleased and wished to keep him, but Hongli firmly declined and was richly supplied with gifts and provisions.

sentences.zh: 至京師，所善李觀病且死，弘禮殫褚為治喪，葬畢乃去。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital his friend Li Guan was ill and near death. Hongli exhausted his resources to arrange the funeral and only left after the burial was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital his friend Li Guan was ill and near death. Hongli exhausted his resources to arrange the funeral and only left after the burial was complete.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，平判異等。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and received the highest grade in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and received the highest grade in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 靈武李欒表為判官，以親老不應，更署東都留守呂元膺參謀。

translations.literal: Li Luan of Lingwu memorialized to appoint him as judge, but citing his aged parents he did not accept and was instead appointed staff officer to Eastern Capital regent Lu Yuanying.
translations.idiomatic: Li Luan of Lingwu memorialized to appoint him as judge, but citing his aged parents he did not accept and was instead appointed staff officer to Eastern Capital regent Lu Yuanying.

sentences.zh: 時天子討蔡，李師道謀襲洛，脅沮朝廷以釋蔡危。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was campaigning against Cai. Li Shidao plotted to strike Luoyang and intimidate the court into lifting the siege on Cai.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Son of Heaven was campaigning against Cai. Li Shidao plotted to strike Luoyang and intimidate the court into lifting the siege on Cai.

sentences.zh: 弘禮為箝揣賊情，部分設張，東都卒無患。

translations.literal: Hongli restrained and probed the rebels' intentions, deployed forces and made arrangements, and in the end the Eastern Capital suffered no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli restrained and probed the rebels' intentions, deployed forces and made arrangements, and in the end the Eastern Capital suffered no harm.

sentences.zh: 遷留守判官，擢忻、汾二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to regent's judge, then elevated to prefect of Xin and Fen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regent's judge, then elevated to prefect of Xin and Fen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 田弘正請朝，表弘禮徙衛州，兼魏博節度副使。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng requested an audience at court he memorialized to transfer Hongli to Weizhou and appoint him deputy military commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Hongzheng requested an audience at court he memorialized to transfer Hongli to Weizhou and appoint him deputy military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 伐李師道，弘正多所咨逮。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Li Shidao, Tian consulted Hongli extensively.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Shidao, Tian consulted Hongli extensively.

sentences.zh: 還魏博，又表為相州刺史。

translations.literal: Returning to Weibo, Tian again memorialized to appoint him prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Weibo, Tian again memorialized to appoint him prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，張弘靖鎮幽州，詔弘禮往副。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, when Zhang Hongjing garrisoned Youzhou, the court ordered Hongli to go as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Changqing, when Zhang Hongjing garrisoned Youzhou, the court ordered Hongli to go as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 未及行，軍亂，改絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Before he could depart the army mutinied, and he was reassigned as prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart the army mutinied, and he was reassigned as prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 李反於汴，詔徙河南尹，倚以捍賊。

translations.literal: When Li rebelled at Bian, the court ordered him transferred to Intendant of Henan, relying on him to repel the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Li rebelled at Bian, the court ordered him transferred to Intendant of Henan, relying on him to repel the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遷河陽節度使，治河內秦渠，溉田千頃，歲收八萬斛。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Heyang, repaired the Qin Canal in Henei, irrigated a thousand qing of fields, and harvested eighty thousand hu per year.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Heyang, repaired the Qin Canal in Henei, irrigated a thousand qing of fields, and harvested eighty thousand hu per year.

sentences.zh: 徙華州刺史，改天平節度使。

translations.literal: He was moved to prefect of Huazhou, then changed to military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to prefect of Huazhou, then changed to military commissioner of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 李同捷叛，與李聽合師討之。

translations.literal: When Li Tongjie rebelled, he joined Li Ting in a combined force to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tongjie rebelled, he joined Li Ting in a combined force to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 至濮州，大將李萬瑀、劉寀擁兵自固，弘禮表萬瑀守沂州，寀守黃州，奪其兵，擊賊禹城，破之，獲鎧裝數十萬。

translations.literal: Reaching Puzhou, the generals Li Wanyu and Liu Cai held troops to fortify themselves. Hongli memorialized to assign Wanyu to defend Yizhou and Cai to defend Huangzhou, stripped them of their soldiers, attacked the rebels at Yucheng, defeated them, and captured several hundred thousand sets of armor.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Puzhou, the generals Li Wanyu and Liu Cai held troops to fortify themselves. Hongli memorialized to assign Wanyu to defend Yizhou and Cai to defend Huangzhou, stripped them of their soldiers, attacked the rebels at Yucheng, defeated them, and captured several hundred thousand sets of armor.

sentences.zh: 時徐泗節度使王智興檄兗、海、鄆、曹、淄、青當徐道者，出車五千乘，轉粟饋軍，弘禮度道遠，乃自兗開盲山故渠，自黃隊抵青丘，師人大濟。

translations.literal: At that time Xuzhou-Suzhou military commissioner Wang Zhixing ordered Yan, Hai, Yun, Cao, Zi, and Qing circuits on the route to Xuzhou to supply five thousand carts to transport grain and feed the army. Hongli judged the route too long, so he reopened the old Blind Mountain canal from Yan, from Huangdui to Qingqiu, and the army was greatly aided.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xuzhou-Suzhou military commissioner Wang Zhixing ordered Yan, Hai, Yun, Cao, Zi, and Qing circuits on the route to Xuzhou to supply five thousand carts to transport grain and feed the army. Hongli judged the route too long, so he reopened the old Blind Mountain canal from Yan, from Huangdui to Qingqiu, and the army was greatly aided.

sentences.zh: 李祐以鄭滑兵三千入齊而潰，弘禮悉斬之，為出鄆兵二千，祐遂大破賊，屍藉十餘里，祐望鄆拜曰：「活我者崔公也！」

translations.literal: Li You led three thousand Zheng-Slide troops into Qi and they collapsed in rout. Hongli had them all executed, then provided two thousand Yun troops. You thereupon routed the rebels decisively, with corpses piled over ten li. You looked toward Yun, bowed, and said: "The one who saved me was Lord Cui!"
translations.idiomatic: Li You led three thousand Zheng-Slide troops into Qi and they collapsed in rout. Hongli had them all executed, then provided two thousand Yun troops. You thereupon routed the rebels decisively, with corpses piled over ten li. You looked toward Yun, bowed, and said, "The one who saved me was Lord Cui!

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書左僕射，徙東都留守。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and transferred to Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and transferred to Eastern Capital regent.

sentences.zh: 召還，以病自乞，改刑部尚書，復為留守。

translations.literal: He was recalled, pleaded illness and requested retirement, was changed to Minister of Justice, and again served as regent.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, pleaded illness and requested retirement, was changed to Minister of Justice, and again served as regent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-five and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five and was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 弘禮短於治民，少愛利，晚頗務多積，素議訿之。

translations.literal: Hongli was deficient in governing the people, showed little concern for profit and benefit, and in his later years devoted himself greatly to accumulation. Public opinion had long criticized him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Hongli was deficient in governing the people, showed little concern for profit and benefit, and in his later years devoted himself greatly to accumulation. Public opinion had long criticized him for this.

sentences.zh: 崔玄亮，字晦叔，磁州昭義人。

translations.literal: Cui Xuanliang, whose courtesy name was Huishu, was a man of Zhaoyi in Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuanliang, courtesy name Huishu, was a native of Zhaoyi in Cizhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，擢進士第，累署諸鎮幕府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he passed the jinshi examination and successively served on the staffs of various military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he passed the jinshi examination and successively served on the staffs of various military commissions.

sentences.zh: 父喪，客高郵，臥苫終制，地下濕，因得痹病，不樂進取。

translations.literal: When his father died he sojourned at Gaoyou, slept on the mourning mat through the full mourning period, and because the ground was damp contracted a crippling illness. He took no pleasure in advancing his career.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he sojourned at Gaoyou, slept on the mourning mat through the full mourning period, and because the ground was damp contracted a crippling illness. He took no pleasure in advancing his career.

sentences.zh: 元和初，召為監察御史，累轉駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned as Investigating Censor and successively transferred to Vice Director in the Department of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was summoned as Investigating Censor and successively transferred to Vice Director in the Department of Transport.

sentences.zh: 清慎介特，淡如也。

translations.literal: He was pure, cautious, upright, and exceptional, plain and unassuming.
translations.idiomatic: He was pure, cautious, upright, and exceptional, plain and unassuming.

sentences.zh: 稍遷密歙二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to prefect of Mi and She prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to prefect of Mi and She prefectures.

sentences.zh: 歙人馬牛生駒犢，官籍蹄噭，故吏得為奸，玄亮焚其籍，一不問。

translations.literal: When horses and cattle in She gave birth to foals and calves, officials registered their hooves and branding for taxation, enabling clerks to commit abuses. Xuanliang burned the registers and made no inquiries at all.
translations.idiomatic: When horses and cattle in She gave birth to foals and calves, officials registered their hooves and branding for taxation, enabling clerks to commit abuses. Xuanliang burned the registers and made no inquiries at all.

sentences.zh: 民山處，輸租者苦之，下令許計斛輸錢，民賴其利。

translations.literal: The people lived in mountainous areas and found it painful to deliver rent in kind. He issued an order permitting payment in cash by measured bushel, and the people benefited from it.
translations.idiomatic: The people lived in mountainous areas and found it painful to deliver rent in kind. He issued an order permitting payment in cash by measured bushel, and the people benefited from it.

sentences.zh: 歷湖、曹二州，辭曹不拜。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Hu and Cao prefectures and declined to accept Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Hu and Cao prefectures and declined to accept Cao.

sentences.zh: 大和四年，繇太常少卿改諫議大夫，朝廷推為宿望，拜右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dahe, from Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he was changed to Remonstrance Grandee. The court regarded him as a veteran of standing and appointed him Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dahe, from Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he was changed to Remonstrance Grandee. The court regarded him as a veteran of standing and appointed him Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 每遷官，輒讓形於色。

translations.literal: With every promotion he showed reluctance upon his face.
translations.idiomatic: With every promotion he showed reluctance upon his face.

sentences.zh: 鄭註構宋申錫，捕逮倉卒，內外震駭。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu framed Song Shenxi; the arrest was sudden and the inner and outer courts were shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu framed Song Shenxi. The arrest was sudden and the inner and outer courts were shaken with alarm.

sentences.zh: 玄亮率諫官叩延英苦諍，反復數百言，文宗未諭，玄亮置笏在陛曰：「孟軻有言：『眾人皆曰殺之，未可也；

translations.literal: Xuanliang led the remonstrance officials to knock at the Yanying Gate and remonstrate bitterly, repeating his words hundreds of times. When Emperor Wenzong did not understand, Xuanliang placed his tablet on the steps and said: "Mencius said: 'When all the common people say he should be killed, it is not yet acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanliang led the remonstrance officials to knock at the Yanying Gate and remonstrate bitterly, repeating his words hundreds of times. When Emperor Wenzong did not understand, Xuanliang placed his tablet on the steps and said, "Mencius said, 'When all the common people say he should be killed, it is not yet acceptable;

sentences.zh: 卿大夫皆曰殺之，未可也；

translations.literal: when all the ministers and grandees say he should be killed, it is not yet acceptable;
translations.idiomatic: when all the ministers and grandees say he should be killed, it is not yet acceptable;

sentences.zh: 天下皆曰殺之，然後察之，乃寘於法。』

translations.literal: when all under Heaven say he should be killed, then examine the matter — only then may he be placed within the law.
translations.idiomatic: when all under Heaven say he should be killed, then examine the matter. Only then may he be placed within the law.

sentences.zh: 今殺一凡庶，當稽典律，況欲誅宰相乎？

translations.literal: To kill an ordinary commoner today requires consulting the statutes and laws — how much more so when one wishes to execute a chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: To kill an ordinary commoner today requires consulting the statutes and laws. How much more so when one wishes to execute a chancellor?

sentences.zh: 臣為陛下惜天下法，不為申錫言也。」

translations.literal: Your servant grieves for Your Majesty's laws under Heaven — not for Shenxi's sake.'
translations.idiomatic: Your servant grieves for Your Majesty's laws under Heaven, not for Shenxi's sake.'

sentences.zh: 俯伏流涕，帝感悟，眾亦服其不橈，由此名重朝廷。

translations.literal: He prostrated himself and wept; the emperor was deeply moved, and the assembly also admired his refusal to yield. From this his reputation weighed heavily at court.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself and wept. The emperor was deeply moved, and the assembly also admired his refusal to yield. From this his reputation weighed heavily at court.

sentences.zh: 頃之，移疾歸東都，召為虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he pleaded illness and returned to the Eastern Capital; he was later summoned and appointed prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he pleaded illness and returned to the Eastern Capital. He was later summoned and appointed prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-six and was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 玄亮晚好黃老清靜術，故所居官未久輒去。

translations.literal: In his later years Xuanliang came to favor the quietist arts of Huang-Lao Daoism; therefore in whatever office he held he did not remain long before departing.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Xuanliang came to favor the quietist arts of Huang-Lao Daoism, and so in whatever office he held he seldom remained long before departing.

sentences.zh: 遺言：「山東士人利便近，皆葬兩都，吾族未嘗遷，當歸葬滏陽，正首丘之義。」

translations.literal: His final instructions read: "Scholars east of the mountains, finding convenience in proximity, all bury themselves in the two capitals. Our clan has never moved away; I should be returned for burial at Feyang — the proper meaning of returning one's head to its mound.'
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions read: "Scholars east of the mountains, finding convenience in proximity, all bury themselves in the two capitals. Our clan has never moved away; I should be returned for burial at Feyang — the proper meaning of returning one's head to its mound.'

sentences.zh: 諸子如命。

translations.literal: His sons carried out his command.
translations.idiomatic: His sons carried out his command.

sentences.zh: 王質，字華卿。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi, whose courtesy name was Huaqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi, courtesy name Huaqing.

sentences.zh: 五世祖通為隋大儒。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Tong was a great Confucian scholar of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Tong was a great Confucian scholar of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 質少孤，客壽春，力耕以養母。

translations.literal: Zhi lost his father while young, lived as a guest in Shouchun, and labored at farming to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi lost his father while young, lived as a guest in Shouchun, and labored at farming to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 講學不倦，諸生從授業者甚眾。

translations.literal: He lectured on learning without tiring; very many students came to receive instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured tirelessly, and very many students came to receive instruction from him.

sentences.zh: 年逾四十，偃蹇無進取意，姻友苦勸以仕，乃舉進士，中甲科。

translations.literal: After he passed forty he remained aloof and had no ambition to advance; relatives and friends repeatedly urged him to enter office, whereupon he entered the Jinshi examination and placed in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: After he passed forty he remained aloof and had no ambition to advance. Relatives and friends repeatedly urged him to enter office, whereupon he sat for the Jinshi examination and placed in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 繇秘書省正字累佐帥府，五遷侍御史，繇山南西道節度副使再轉諫議大夫。

translations.literal: From Proofreader in the Secretariat he successively served as aide in commanders' headquarters, was promoted five times to Attending Censor, and from Vice Commissioner of the Shannan West Circuit was again transferred to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: From proofreader in the Secretariat he successively served as aide in commanders' headquarters, was promoted five times to Attending Censor, and from vice commissioner of the Shannan West Circuit was again transferred to Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 宋申錫之得罪，質與諫官伏閣，文宗開延英召見，泣涕陳諫，帝稍寤，申錫得不死。

translations.literal: When Song Shenxi fell into guilt, Zhi and the remonstrance officials lay prostrate at the gate; Emperor Wenzong opened the Yanying Hall and summoned them. Weeping, Zhi presented his remonstrance; the emperor gradually came to his senses, and Shenxi was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Shenxi fell into disgrace, Zhi and the remonstrance officials lay prostrate at the gate. Emperor Wenzong opened the Yanying Hall and summoned them. Weeping, Zhi presented his remonstrance; the emperor gradually came to his senses, and Shenxi was spared death.

sentences.zh: 為宦豎所惡，出虢州刺史。

translations.literal: Hated by the eunuch faction, he was sent out as prefect of Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Hated by the eunuch faction, he was sent out as prefect of Guo.

sentences.zh: 李德裕素器之，擢給事中、河南尹，徙宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Li Deyu had long valued him; he was promoted to Supervising Secretary and Intendant of Henan, then transferred to Commissioner of the Xuan-She Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu had long valued him. He was promoted to Supervising Secretary and Intendant of Henan, then transferred to commissioner of the Xuan-She Circuit.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈左散騎常侍，謚曰定。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-eight, was posthumously awarded Left Regular Attendant, and was given the posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-eight, was posthumously awarded Left Regular Attendant, and was given the posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 質清白畏慎，為政必先究風俗，所至有惠愛。

translations.literal: Zhi was pure, cautious, and reverent in conduct; in governing he always first investigated local customs, and wherever he went he showed kindness and care.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was pure, cautious, and reverent in conduct. In governing he always first investigated local customs, and wherever he went he showed kindness and care.

sentences.zh: 雖與德裕厚善，而中立自將，不為黨。

translations.literal: Although he was on close terms with Deyu, he held himself neutrally and did not join a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Although he was on close terms with Deyu, he held himself neutrally and did not join a faction.

sentences.zh: 奏署幕府者，若河東裴夷直、天水趙皙、隴西李行方、梁國劉蕡，皆一時選云。

translations.literal: Those he memorialized for appointment to his staff — such as Pei Yizhi of Hedong, Zhao Xi of Tianshui, Li Xingfang of Longxi, and Liu Fen of Liang — were all outstanding men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Those he memorialized for appointment to his staff — such as Pei Yizhi of Hedong, Zhao Xi of Tianshui, Li Xingfang of Longxi, and Liu Fen of Liang — were all outstanding men of the age.

sentences.zh: 殷侑，陳州人。

translations.literal: Yin You, a man of Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yin You was a native of Chen prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼有誌於學，不治資產。

translations.literal: From youth he was resolved upon learning and did not manage family property.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was resolved upon learning and did not manage family property.

sentences.zh: 長通經術，以講道為娛。

translations.literal: As he grew he mastered the classics and took lecturing on the Way as his recreation.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he mastered the classics and took lecturing on the Way as his recreation.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，及五經第，其學長於《禮》，擢太常博士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he passed the Five Classics examination; his learning excelled in the Rites, and he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he passed the Five Classics examination. His learning excelled in the Rites, and he was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 元和八年，回鶻請和親，朝廷以仰費廣劇，欲紓以期。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe the Uyghurs requested a marriage alliance; the court, because the expense borne upward was vast and severe, wished to defer it for a time.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe the Uyghurs requested a marriage alliance. The court, because the expense borne upward was vast and severe, wished to defer it for a time.

sentences.zh: 詔侑、宗正少卿李孝誠使回鶻，可汗驕甚，盛陳甲兵，欲臣使者，侑不為屈。

translations.literal: An edict ordered You and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Li Xiaocheng to go as envoys to the Uyghurs. The qaghan was extremely arrogant, arrayed armor and troops in great display, and wished to make the envoys submit — but You would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered You and Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Li Xiaocheng to go as envoys to the Uyghurs. The qaghan was extremely arrogant, arrayed armor and troops in great display, and wished to make the envoys submit — but You would not yield.

sentences.zh: 已傳命，虜責其倨，宣言欲留不遣，眾色怖，侑徐曰：「可汗，唐婿，欲坐屈使者拜，乃可汗無禮，非使臣倨也。」

translations.literal: After the imperial message had been delivered, the barbarians reproached him for arrogance and declared they intended to detain him and not send him back. The company looked terrified. You said calmly: "Qaghan, you are Tang's son-in-law. If you wish to remain seated and force the envoy to bow, that is the qaghan's lack of courtesy — not the envoy's arrogance.'
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial message had been delivered, the barbarians reproached him for arrogance and declared they intended to detain him and not send him back. The company looked terrified. You said calmly, "Qaghan, you are Tang's son-in-law. If you wish to remain seated and force the envoy to bow, that is the qaghan's lack of courtesy — not the envoy's arrogance.'

sentences.zh: 虜憚其言，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The barbarians feared his words and did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians feared his words and did not dare press him.

sentences.zh: 還，遷虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 王承宗叛，遣侑招諭，承宗聽命。

translations.literal: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, You was sent to summon and instruct him; Chengzong obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong rebelled, You was sent to summon and instruct him, and Chengzong obeyed the command.

sentences.zh: 進諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 侑論朝廷治亂得失，前後凡八十四通，以語切，出為桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: You discussed the gains and losses in the court's order and disorder, submitting eighty-four memorials in all; because his language was sharp, he was sent out as Commissioner of the Gui Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: You discussed the gains and losses in the court's order and disorder, submitting eighty-four memorials in all. Because his language was sharp, he was sent out as commissioner of the Gui Circuit.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年，徙江西。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoli he was transferred to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoli he was transferred to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 所至以潔廉稱。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he was known for purity and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he was known for purity and integrity.

sentences.zh: 入為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，李同捷叛，而王廷湊陰為唇齒，兵久不解，詔五品以上官議尚書省。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Li Tongjie rebelled, while Wang Tingcou secretly acted as his mutual support; the troops were long unable to achieve resolution. An edict ordered officials of the fifth rank and above to deliberate at the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Li Tongjie rebelled, while Wang Tingcou secretly acted as his mutual support. The troops were long unable to achieve resolution. An edict ordered officials of the fifth rank and above to deliberate at the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝銳欲討賊，群臣無敢異論者，獨侑請舍廷湊而專事同捷，且言：「願以宗社安危為計，善師攻心為武，含垢安人為遠圖，網漏吞舟為至誡。」

translations.literal: The emperor was keen to attack the rebels; none among the ministers dared offer a differing view — only You asked to set Tingcou aside and concentrate on Tongjie, saying moreover: "I wish to take the safety of the altars of state as the measure, to make winning hearts the best martial art, to bear disgrace and settle the people as the long view, and to let the net leak so that great fish may pass as the highest admonition.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was keen to attack the rebels; none among the ministers dared offer a differing view — only You asked to set Tingcou aside and concentrate on Tongjie, saying moreover, "I wish to take the safety of the altars of state as the measure, to make winning hearts the best martial art, to bear disgrace and settle the people as the long view, and to let the net leak so that great fish may pass as the highest admonition.'

sentences.zh: 帝不納，然內嘉尚。

translations.literal: The emperor did not adopt it, yet inwardly he admired it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not adopt it, yet inwardly he admired it.

sentences.zh: 同捷平，以侑嘗為滄州行軍司馬，遂拜義昌軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Tongjie was pacified, because You had once served as marching army adjutant at Cangzhou, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongjie was pacified, because You had once served as marching army adjutant at Cangzhou, he was appointed military commissioner of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 於時痍荒之餘，骸骨蔽野，墟裏生荊棘，侑單身之官，安足粗淡，與下共勞苦，以仁惠為治。

translations.literal: At that time, in the aftermath of devastation and desolation, bones covered the fields and brambles grew in ruined villages. You went to his post alone, content with coarse fare, shared toil and hardship with those below him, and governed through kindness and grace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, in the aftermath of devastation and desolation, bones covered the fields and brambles grew in ruined villages. You went to his post alone, content with coarse fare, shared toil and hardship with those below him, and governed through kindness and grace.

sentences.zh: 歲中，流戶繈屬而還，遂為營田，丐耕牛三萬，詔度支賜帛四萬匹佐其市。

translations.literal: Within the year, displaced households returned in continuous streams. He then established military colonies and requested thirty thousand plow oxen; an edict ordered the Directorate of the Treasury to grant forty thousand bolts of silk to assist in purchasing them.
translations.idiomatic: Within the year, displaced households returned in continuous streams. He then established military colonies and requested thirty thousand plow oxen. An edict ordered the Directorate of the Treasury to grant forty thousand bolts of silk to assist in purchasing them.

sentences.zh: 初，州兵三萬，仰稟度支，侑始至一歲，自以賦入贍其半，二歲則周用，乃奏罷度支所賜。

translations.literal: At first the prefecture's thirty thousand troops depended on rations from the Directorate of the Treasury. In You's first year after arrival, tax revenues themselves supplied half their needs; in the second year expenditures were fully covered, whereupon he memorialized to abolish the grants from the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: At first the prefecture's thirty thousand troops depended on rations from the Directorate of the Treasury. In You's first year after arrival, tax revenues themselves supplied half their needs; in the second year expenditures were fully covered, whereupon he memorialized to abolish the grants from the Directorate.

sentences.zh: 戶口滋饒，廥儲盈腐，上下便安，請立石紀政。

translations.literal: Household registers grew abundant, granaries overflowed until grain rotted, superiors and inferiors alike found ease and security, and he requested that a stele be erected to record his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers grew abundant, granaries overflowed until grain rotted, superiors and inferiors alike found ease and security, and he requested that a stele be erected to record his governance.

sentences.zh: 以勞加檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: For his labors he was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: For his labors he was additionally appointed acting Minister of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙天平節度。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Tianping command.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Tianping command.

sentences.zh: 自李師道亂，朝廷雖析三鎮，然務安反側，賦入盡為軍資，無輸王府者。

translations.literal: Since Li Shidao's rebellion, although the court had divided the three commands, it still sought to pacify the restless; tax revenues all went to military supplies, with none submitted to the imperial treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Since Li Shidao's rebellion, although the court had divided the three commands, it still sought to pacify the restless. Tax revenues all went to military supplies, with none submitted to the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 侑以餉軍有贏，當上送官，乃裁制經費，歲以錢十五萬緡、粟五萬石歸有司。

translations.literal: You, finding that army provisions had a surplus that ought to be sent up to the government, trimmed expenditures and each year returned one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash and fifty thousand shi of grain to the appropriate offices.
translations.idiomatic: You, finding that army provisions had a surplus that ought to be sent up to the government, trimmed expenditures and each year returned one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash and fifty thousand shi of grain to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫溫造劾侑違制，擅賦斂民為無名之獻，詔以庾承宣代還。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao impeached You for violating regulations and levying taxes on the people without authorization as an unscheduled tribute. An edict ordered Yu Chengxuan to replace him and recall him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao impeached You for violating regulations and levying taxes on the people without authorization as an unscheduled tribute. An edict ordered Yu Chengxuan to replace him and recall him.

sentences.zh: 會濮州掾崔元武受吏賕，又率屬邑奉錢，增私馬估售官，疊三罪計絹百二十匹。

translations.literal: It happened that Pu prefecture aide Cui Yuanwu accepted bribes from officials, also led subordinate districts in presenting money, and inflated the appraised value of his private horses to sell them to the government — three offenses stacked together, totaling one hundred twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Pu prefecture aide Cui Yuanwu accepted bribes from officials, also led subordinate districts in presenting money, and inflated the appraised value of his private horses to sell them to the government — three offenses stacked together, totaling one hundred twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 大理以入私馬一重，削三官，刑部覆訊當流，未決。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review, taking the private-horse offense as the gravest, stripped three ranks; the Ministry of Justice on re-examination found exile appropriate — the case was undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review, taking the private-horse offense as the gravest, stripped three ranks. The Ministry of Justice on re-examination found exile appropriate — the case was undecided.

sentences.zh: 侑奏：「三犯不同，坐所重。

translations.literal: You memorialized: "The three offenses differ; one should be punished for the gravest.
translations.idiomatic: You memorialized, "The three offenses differ; one should be punished for the gravest.

sentences.zh: 律，頻贓者累論。

translations.literal: The law states that repeated offenses involving illicit gains are to be judged cumulatively.
translations.idiomatic: The law states that repeated offenses involving illicit gains are to be judged cumulatively.

sentences.zh: 元武犯皆枉法，當死。」

translations.literal: All of Yuanwu's offenses were violations of law and warranted death.'
translations.idiomatic: All of Yuanwu's offenses were violations of law and warranted death.'

sentences.zh: 詔用覆訊，流元武賀州。

translations.literal: An edict adopted the re-examination; Yuanwu was exiled to He prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted the re-examination; Yuanwu was exiled to He prefecture.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉侑守法，進刑部尚書，以造所奏不直，復用為天平節度。

translations.literal: The emperor praised You for upholding the law, promoted him to Minister of Justice, and because Zao's memorial had been unjust, again appointed him to the Tianping command.
