translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised You for upholding the law, promoted him to Minister of Justice, and because Zao's memorial had been unjust, again appointed him to the Tianping command.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，再召為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng he was again summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaicheng he was again summoned as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 時李訓、鄭註已誅，帝問侑治安術，侑言：「朝廷宜任耆德，毋輕用新進。」

translations.literal: At that time Li Xun and Zheng Zhu had already been executed. The emperor asked You about the art of governing for peace and order. You said: "The court ought to employ men of mature virtue and not lightly use newly risen officials.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xun and Zheng Zhu had already been executed. The emperor asked You about the art of governing for peace and order. You said, "The court ought to employ men of mature virtue and not lightly use newly risen officials.'

sentences.zh: 帝善之，賜彩三百匹。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and bestowed three hundred bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and bestowed three hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 初，鹽鐵度支使屬官悉得以罪人系在所獄，或私置牢院，而州縣不聞知，歲千百數，不時決。

translations.literal: Formerly, subordinate officials of the Salt, Iron, and Treasury Commission were all permitted to detain criminals in their own prisons, or to set up private detention yards — while prefectures and counties knew nothing of it. Each year there were hundreds or thousands of such cases, decided not in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, subordinate officials of the Salt, Iron, and Treasury Commission were all permitted to detain criminals in their own prisons, or to set up private detention yards — while prefectures and counties knew nothing of it. Each year there were hundreds or thousands of such cases, decided not in timely fashion.

sentences.zh: 侑奏許州縣糾列所系，申本道觀察使，並具獄上聞。

translations.literal: You memorialized that prefectures and counties be permitted to investigate and report those detained, notify the circuit observation commissioner, and submit the full case records to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: You memorialized that prefectures and counties be permitted to investigate and report those detained, notify the circuit observation commissioner, and submit the full case records to the throne.

sentences.zh: 許之，賜黃金十斤，以酬直言。

translations.literal: It was granted; he was awarded ten jin of gold as reward for his forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: It was granted; he was awarded ten jin of gold as reward for his forthright speech.

sentences.zh: 涇原節度使朱叔夜坐侵牟士卒，贓數萬，家畜兵器，罷為左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Jingyuan Military Commissioner Zhu Shuye was convicted of exploiting and squeezing his soldiers, amassing illicit gains in the tens of thousands, and keeping weapons at home; he was dismissed and made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan Military Commissioner Zhu Shuye was convicted of exploiting and squeezing his soldiers, amassing illicit gains in the tens of thousands, and keeping weapons at home. He was dismissed and made Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 侑薄其罪，天子由是疏之，賜叔夜死，出侑為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: You treated his offense as slight; the Son of Heaven therefore grew distant from him, ordered Shuye to commit suicide, and sent You out as Military Commissioner of Shannan East.
translations.idiomatic: You treated his offense as slight; the Son of Heaven therefore grew distant from him, ordered Shuye to commit suicide, and sent You out as military commissioner of Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 坐減兵不先論啟，左遷太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: For reducing troops without first memorializing and reporting, he was demoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent and assigned to the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: For reducing troops without first memorializing and reporting, he was demoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent and assigned to the Eastern Capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 俄領忠武節度。

translations.literal: Before long he took command of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took command of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two and was posthumously awarded Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two and was posthumously awarded Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 侑以經術進，臨事銳敏，有強直名。

translations.literal: You advanced through classical learning; in handling affairs he was sharp and quick, and had a reputation for forceful uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: You advanced through classical learning. In handling affairs he was sharp and quick, and had a reputation for forceful uprightness.

sentences.zh: 晚節內冀臺輔，稍務交結，而素望少衰云。

translations.literal: In his later years he inwardly hoped for a post among the chief ministers, gradually devoted himself to cultivating connections, and his longstanding reputation somewhat declined — so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he inwardly hoped for a post among the chief ministers, gradually devoted himself to cultivating connections, and his longstanding reputation somewhat declined — so it is said.

sentences.zh: 孫盈孫。

translations.literal: Sun Yingsun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yingsun.

sentences.zh: 侑孫 盈孫盈孫，廣明初，為成都諸曹參軍。

translations.literal: You's grandson Yingsun — Sun Yingsun. At the beginning of the Guangming era he served as adjutant in the various bureaus of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: You's grandson Yingsun. At the beginning of the Guangming era he served as adjutant in the various bureaus of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 僖宗至蜀，聞有禮學，擢太常博士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong arrived in Shu, hearing that he had learning in ritual, he was promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong arrived in Shu, hearing that he had learning in ritual, he was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年，帝將還京，而七廟焚殘，告享無所。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangqi the emperor was about to return to the capital, but the seven ancestral temples had been burned and ruined, and there was nowhere to announce and offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guangqi the emperor was about to return to the capital, but the seven ancestral temples had been burned and ruined, and there was nowhere to announce and offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 盈孫白宰相：「始乘輿西，有司盡載神主以行，至鄠，悉為盜奪。

translations.literal: Yingsun informed the chief ministers: "When the imperial carriage first went west, the responsible offices loaded all the spirit tablets to take along; upon reaching E, they were all seized by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsun informed the chief ministers, "When the imperial carriage first went west, the responsible offices loaded all the spirit tablets to take along; upon reaching E, they were all seized by bandits.

sentences.zh: 今天子還宮，宜前具其禮。」

translations.literal: Now that the Son of Heaven is returning to the palace, the rites ought to be prepared in advance.'
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Son of Heaven is returning to the palace, the rites ought to be prepared in advance.'

sentences.zh: 宰相建言，脩復宗廟，功費廣，請與禮官議。

translations.literal: The chief ministers proposed restoring the ancestral temples, but the labor and expense would be vast; they asked to consult with the ritual officials.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers proposed restoring the ancestral temples, but the labor and expense would be vast; they asked to consult with the ritual officials.

sentences.zh: 時佗博士不在，獨盈孫從，議曰：「故廟十一室，二十三楹，楹十一梁，垣墉廣袤稱之。

translations.literal: At that time the other erudites were absent; Yingsun alone accompanied them and argued: "The former temple had eleven chambers, twenty-three bays; each bay had eleven beams, and the walls' length and breadth matched accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the other erudites were absent; Yingsun alone accompanied them and argued, "The former temple had eleven chambers, twenty-three bays; each bay had eleven beams, and the walls' length and breadth matched accordingly.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷多難，宜少變禮。

translations.literal: Now the court faces many hardships; the rites ought to be slightly modified.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court faces many hardships; the rites ought to be slightly modified.

sentences.zh: 按至德時作神主長安殿，饗告如宗廟，廟成乃祔。

translations.literal: According to precedent, in the Zhide era spirit tablets were made in the Chang'an Hall; offerings and announcements were conducted as at the ancestral temple, and only after the temple was completed were the tablets enshrined.
translations.idiomatic: According to precedent, in the Zhide era spirit tablets were made in the Chang'an Hall; offerings and announcements were conducted as at the ancestral temple, and only after the temple was completed were the tablets enshrined.

sentences.zh: 今正衙外無它殿，伏聞詔旨以少府監寓太廟，請因增完為十一室，其三太后廟，權舍西南夾廡，須廟成議遷。」

translations.literal: Now beyond the main audience hall there is no other hall. I have heard that an edict lodges the Directorate of the Palace Manufactories in the ancestral temple. I ask that it be expanded and completed into eleven chambers; the three chambers for empress dowagers should temporarily be housed in the southwest side galleries, to be relocated once the temple is finished.'
translations.idiomatic: Now beyond the main audience hall there is no other hall. I have heard that an edict lodges the Directorate of the Palace Manufactories in the ancestral temple. I ask that it be expanded and completed into eleven chambers; the three chambers for empress dowagers should temporarily be housed in the southwest side galleries, to be relocated once the temple is finished.'

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 自是神主、樂縣，皆所創定，舊學禮家當其議。

translations.literal: From this the spirit tablets and musical regalia were all newly established by him; veteran ritual scholars of the age were present at the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: From this the spirit tablets and musical regalia were all newly established by him; veteran ritual scholars of the age were present at the deliberation.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年，昭宗郊祠，兩中尉及樞密皆以宰相服侍上。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longji, when Emperor Zhaozong performed the suburban sacrifice, both chief eunuchs and the privy secretaries all attended the emperor dressed as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longji, when Emperor Zhaozong performed the suburban sacrifice, both chief eunuchs and the privy secretaries all attended the emperor dressed as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 盈孫奏言：「先世典令，無內官朝服侍祠。

translations.literal: Yingsun memorialized: "The canonical regulations of former ages contain no provision for inner officials in court dress to attend sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yingsun memorialized, "The canonical regulations of former ages contain no provision for inner officials in court dress to attend sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 必欲之，當隨所攝資品，雖無授據，猶免僭逼。」

translations.literal: If they must attend, they should follow the rank insignia of whatever office they hold in commission; even without formal appointment documents, that would still avoid presumptuous encroachment.'
translations.idiomatic: If they must attend, they should follow the rank insignia of whatever office they hold in commission; even without formal appointment documents, that would still avoid presumptuous encroachment.'

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 時喪亂後，制度雕紊，追補容典，皆盈孫折衷焉。

translations.literal: At that time, after the years of chaos and ruin, institutions were worn and disordered; in restoring and supplementing ceremonial regulations, Yingsun adjudicated them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, after the years of chaos and ruin, institutions were worn and disordered. In restoring and supplementing ceremonial regulations, Yingsun adjudicated them all.

sentences.zh: 終大理卿，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and was posthumously awarded Minister of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and was posthumously awarded Minister of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 王彥威，其先出太原。

translations.literal: Wang Yanwei; his forebears came from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanwei's forebears came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，家無資，自力於學。

translations.literal: He lost his father while young; the family had no means, and he relied on his own strength in study.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father while young. The family had no means, and he relied on his own strength in study.

sentences.zh: 舉明經甲科。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 淹識古今典禮，未得調，求為太常散吏，卿知其經生，補檢討官。

translations.literal: He was thoroughly versed in ancient and modern ceremonial codes. Having received no appointment, he requested to serve as a clerk in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; the director, knowing him to be a classical scholar, appointed him reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was thoroughly versed in ancient and modern ceremonial codes. Having received no appointment, he requested to serve as a clerk in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. The director, knowing him to be a classical scholar, appointed him reviser.

sentences.zh: 彥威采獲隋以來下訖唐凡禮沿革，皆條次匯分，號《元和新禮》上之。

translations.literal: Yanwei gathered all changes in ritual from the Sui down through Tang, arranged and classified them by item, titled the work New Rites of the Yuanhe Era, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei gathered all changes in ritual from the Sui down through Tang, arranged and classified them by item, titled the work New Rites of the Yuanhe Era, and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 有詔拜博士。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him erudite.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以正月崩，有司議葬用十二月下宿，彥威建言：「天子之葬七月，《春秋》之義。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong died in the first month; the responsible offices debated burying him in the twelfth month during the lower lodging period. Yanwei proposed: "A Son of Heaven is buried in the seventh month — such is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong died in the first month; the responsible offices debated burying him in the twelfth month during the lower lodging period. Yanwei proposed, "A Son of Heaven is buried in the seventh month — such is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 誌崩不誌葬，必其時也。

translations.literal: It records death but does not record burial — burial must come at the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: It records death but does not record burial — burial must come at the proper time.

sentences.zh: 舉天下葬一人，故過期不葬則譏之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven buries one man; therefore if burial passes the proper period, it is reproached.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven buries one man; therefore if burial passes the proper period, it is reproached.

sentences.zh: 高祖、中宗葬皆六月，太宗四月，高宗九月，睿、代二宗皆五月，德宗十月，順宗七月，惟玄、肅二宗皆十二月，有為為之，非常典也。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Zhongzong were both buried in the sixth month; Taizong in the fourth; Gaozong in the ninth; Ruizong and Daizong both in the fifth; Dezong in the tenth; Shunzong in the seventh; only Xuanzong and Suzong were both buried in the twelfth month — acts of deliberate choice, not regular canonical practice.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Zhongzong were both buried in the sixth month; Taizong in the fourth; Gaozong in the ninth; Ruizong and Daizong both in the fifth; Dezong in the tenth; Shunzong in the seventh; only Xuanzong and Suzong were both buried in the twelfth month — acts of deliberate choice, not regular canonical practice.

sentences.zh: 且葬畢而虞，虞而卒哭，卒哭而祔，皆卜日。

translations.literal: Moreover, after burial comes the yu rite; after yu comes the final wailing; after the final wailing comes enshrinement — each requires selecting an auspicious day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after burial comes the yu rite; after yu comes the final wailing; after the final wailing comes enshrinement — each requires selecting an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 今葬卜歲暮，則畢祔在明年正月，是改元慶賜皆廢矣。」

translations.literal: If burial is now set for year's end, then the completion of enshrinement would fall in the first month of the next year — and the new reign year's celebrations and bestowals would all be abandoned.'
translations.idiomatic: If burial is now set for year's end, then the completion of enshrinement would fall in the first month of the next year — and the new reign year's celebrations and bestowals would all be abandoned.'

sentences.zh: 有詔更用五月。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that the fifth month be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that the fifth month be used instead.

sentences.zh: 淮南李夷簡上言：「大行皇帝功高，宜稱祖。」

translations.literal: Li Yijian of Huainan submitted a memorial: "The late emperor's achievements were lofty; he ought to be styled zu."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yijian of Huainan submitted a memorial: "The late emperor's achievements were so great that he ought to be styled as founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 穆宗下其議，彥威奏：「古者始封為太祖，由太祖而降，則又祖有功，宗有德。

translations.literal: Muzong referred the proposal for deliberation. Yanwei memorialized: "In antiquity the first enfeoffed was styled Taizu; descending from Taizu, zu honored merit and zong honored virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong referred the matter for deliberation. Yanwei memorialized, "In antiquity the first enfeoffed ruler was styled Grand Ancestor; thereafter, zu honored merit and zong honored virtue.

sentences.zh: 故夏人祖顓頊而宗禹，商人祖契而宗湯，周人祖文王而宗武王。

translations.literal: Thus the Xia made Zhuanxu zu and Yu zong; the Shang made Qi zu and Tang zong; the Zhou made King Wen zu and King Wu zong.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Xia honored Zhuanxu as zu and Yu as zong; the Shang honored Qi as zu and Tang as zong; the Zhou honored King Wen as zu and King Wu as zong.

sentences.zh: 魏晉而下，務欲推美，自始祖外並建列祖之議，叔世亂象，不可以為訓。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward, all strove to extend praise; apart from the founding ancestor they together established the proposal of ranking multiple zu — a decadent-age disorder not fit to serve as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, rulers strove to heap posthumous praise upon their forebears; aside from the founding ancestor, they established multiple zu in succession — the disorder of a decadent age, unfit to serve as instruction.

sentences.zh: 唐本周禮，以景皇帝為太祖，祖神堯而宗太宗，自高宗後鹹稱宗，以為成法。

translations.literal: Tang originally followed the Rites of Zhou, taking Emperor Jing as Taizu, making Shenyao zu and Taizong zong; from Gaozong onward all were styled zong, taken as established law.
translations.idiomatic: Tang originally followed the Rites of Zhou, taking Emperor Jing as Grand Ancestor, honoring Shenyao as zu and Taizong as zong; from Gaozong onward every emperor was styled zong — this became fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 不然，太宗致升平，玄宗清內難，肅宗收復兩都，皆撥亂反正，猶不稱祖。

translations.literal: If not so, Taizong brought about the Ascendant Peace, Xuanzong cleared internal troubles, Suzong recovered the two capitals — all restored order from chaos and returned to the right way — yet none was styled zu.
translations.idiomatic: After all, Taizong had brought the realm to ascendancy, Xuanzong had quelled internal strife, Suzong had recovered the two capitals — each had restored order from chaos — yet none was styled zu.

sentences.zh: 今當本三代之制，黜魏晉亂法，大行廟號宜稱宗。」

translations.literal: Now one ought to take the institutions of the Three Dynasties as root, dismiss the disorderly law of Wei and Jin; the late emperor's temple name ought to be styled zong."
translations.idiomatic: We ought now to return to the institutions of the Three Dynasties and reject the corrupted practices of Wei and Jin; the late emperor's temple name should be zong."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又舊事，祔廟必告於太極殿，然後奉主入廟，既事則已，而有司祔主畢，又還告太極殿。

translations.literal: Again, by old practice, upon enshrining in the temple one must announce at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, then convey the spirit tablet into the temple; once the rite was done it ended — yet the responsible offices, after completing the enshrinement, again returned to announce at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: By older custom, enshrining a spirit tablet required first announcing the rite at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, then conveying the tablet into the ancestral temple — and that should have been the end of it. Yet the responsible offices, after completing the enshrinement, again returned to announce at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 彥威以為不可，執政怒，坐祝辭誤，奪二季俸，削一階。

translations.literal: Yanwei held it unacceptable; the chief ministers grew angry; on the charge of an error in the sacrificial prayer, they stripped him of two seasons' salary and demoted him one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei held this improper. The chief ministers were enraged; citing an error in a sacrificial prayer, they stripped him of two seasons' salary and demoted him one rank.

sentences.zh: 彥威終不回屈。

translations.literal: Yanwei in the end never yielded or bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei never yielded.

sentences.zh: 後累擢司封郎中、弘文館學士、諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly promoted to bureau director of enfeoffments, academician of the Hongwen Academy, and remonstrance and policy advisor.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted in succession to bureau director in the Office of Enfeoffments, academician of the Hongwen Academy, and remonstrance and policy advisor.

sentences.zh: 李師道既平，其十二州賦法未均，詔彥威為勘定兩稅使，差量纖悉，人不為煩。

translations.literal: After Li Shidao was pacified, the tax laws of his twelve prefectures were not yet equalized; an edict appointed Yanwei commissioner to assess and fix the two-tax system; his calculations were meticulous in every detail, and the people were not vexed.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao's rebellion was crushed, the tax assessments of his twelve prefectures remained unequal. Yanwei was appointed commissioner to assess and standardize the two-tax system. His calculations were meticulous, yet the people found the process no burden.

sentences.zh: 還，兼史館修撰。

translations.literal: Upon return, he concurrently served as historiography compiler.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made a concurrent historiography compiler.

sentences.zh: 興平民上官興殺人亡命，吏囚其父。

translations.literal: Shangguan Xing of Xingping killed a man and fled for his life; officials imprisoned his father.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Xing of Xingping killed a man and fled. Officials imprisoned his father.

sentences.zh: 興聞，自首請罪。

translations.literal: Xing heard of it and surrendered himself to confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing learned of this, he turned himself in to confess his crime.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹杜悰、御史中丞宇文鼎以自歸死免父之囚，可勸風俗，議減死。

translations.literal: Capital Protector Du Cong and censor-in-chief Yuwen Ding held that surrendering oneself to accept death to free one's imprisoned father could encourage custom and morality; they proposed reducing the death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: The Capital Protector Du Cong and Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding argued that surrendering oneself to face execution in order to free one's father would encourage filial conduct; they proposed commuting the death sentence.

sentences.zh: 彥威上言：「殺人者死，百王共守。

translations.literal: Yanwei submitted a memorial: "He who kills shall die — all kings through the ages jointly uphold this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei memorialized, "He who kills shall die — all kings through the ages have upheld this principle.

sentences.zh: 原而不殺，是教殺人。」

translations.literal: To pardon and not kill is to teach killing."
translations.idiomatic: To pardon instead of executing him is to teach men they may kill with impunity.

sentences.zh: 有詔貸死，彥威詣宰相據法爭論，下遷河南少尹。

translations.literal: An edict granted reprieve from death; Yanwei went to the chief ministers and argued on the basis of law; he was demoted and reassigned as vice prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commuted the death sentence. Yanwei went to the chief ministers and argued the matter on legal grounds. He was demoted to vice prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 俄改司農卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was reassigned minister of revenue for agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reassigned as Minister of Revenue for Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔執政，雅善之，進拜平盧節度使。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin held power, he had always favored him well; he was promoted and appointed military commissioner of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin, then chief minister, had long favored him and had him promoted to military commissioner of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 開成初，召為戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng, he was summoned as vice minister of revenue and put in charge of the Bureau of Public Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng reign he was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue and given charge of the Bureau of Public Revenue.

sentences.zh: 彥威於儒學固該邃，亦善吏事，但經總財用，出入米鹽，非所長也。

translations.literal: Yanwei in Confucian learning was indeed comprehensive and profound; he was also skilled in clerical affairs — but overseeing finances, the comings and goings of grain and salt, was not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei was thoroughly versed in Confucian learning and skilled in administrative matters, but overseeing state finances — the daily flow of grain and salt — was not his forte.

sentences.zh: 而性剛訐自恃，嘗見文宗，顯奏曰：「百口家知有歲計，而軍用一切不可謹邪？

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was rigid, contentious, and self-reliant; once when he had audience with Emperor Wenzong he stated plainly in memorial: "A household of a hundred mouths knows there must be an annual budget — can military expenditures of every sort not be managed with care?
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was rigid and self-assured. Once, in audience with Emperor Wenzong, he declared openly, "Even a household of a hundred mouths plans its yearly budget — surely military expenditures can be managed with equal care?

sentences.zh: 臣按見財，量入以為出，隨色占費，終歲用之，無毫厘差。

translations.literal: Your subject inspects the visible wealth, measures income to determine outgo, allocates expenditures item by item, uses it through the year — without a hairsbreadth of discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: I examine the treasury on hand, measure income against outgo, allocate each category of expense, and disburse through the year — not a hairsbreadth off.

sentences.zh: 假令臣一旦迷愚，欲自欺沒，亦不可得。」

translations.literal: Even if your subject one day became confused and foolish, wishing to deceive himself and embezzle, it would still be impossible."
translations.idiomatic: Even if I grew foolish and wished to deceive myself or conceal funds, I could not.

sentences.zh: 因上《占頟圖》。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted the Chart of Allocated Expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon submitted his Chart of Allocated Expenditures.

sentences.zh: 又言：「至德迄元和，天下觀察者十，節度者二十有九，防禦者四，經略者三，大都通邑皆有兵，最凡八十餘萬。

translations.literal: Again he said: "From Zhide to Yuanhe, throughout the realm there were ten regional inspectors, twenty-nine military commissioners, four defense commissioners, three pacification commissioners; great capitals and thoroughfare districts all had troops — in all more than eight hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to say, "From the Zhide era to Yuanhe, the realm counted ten regional inspectors, twenty-nine military commissioners, four defense commissioners, and three pacification commissioners; every major city and thoroughfare district maintained troops — more than eight hundred thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 長慶籍戶三百五十萬，而兵乃九十九萬，率三戶資一兵。

translations.literal: In the Changqing registers there were 3.5 million households, yet troops numbered 990,000 — on average three households supported one soldier.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing the registered households numbered 3.5 million, yet troops stood at 990,000 — on average three households supporting one soldier.

sentences.zh: 今舉天下之入，歲三千五百萬，上供者三之一，又三之二則衣賜仰給焉。

translations.literal: Now taking all income under Heaven, yearly 35 million; one-third was submitted upward; another two-thirds went to clothing stipends and grants on which troops relied.
translations.idiomatic: All revenue under Heaven came to 35 million annually; one-third went to the central government, while two-thirds supplied clothing and stipends for the troops.

sentences.zh: 自留州留使外，余四十萬眾，皆仰度支。」

translations.literal: Apart from what was retained by prefectures and commissioners, the remaining four hundred thousand masses all relied on the Bureau of Public Revenue."
translations.idiomatic: Aside from funds retained locally by prefectures and commissioners, the remaining four hundred thousand men all depended on the Bureau of Public Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又為《供軍圖》上之。

translations.literal: He also composed and submitted the Chart of Army Supply.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted his Chart of Army Supply.

sentences.zh: 彥威雖自謂楗柅奸冒，著定其費，於利害無益也。

translations.literal: Though Yanwei claimed to bolt against fraud and embezzlement and fix expenditures definitively, it was of no benefit to advantage or harm.
translations.idiomatic: For all Yanwei's boasts of blocking fraud and fixing expenditures, the policy did nothing to improve matters.

sentences.zh: 始，神策軍多以稟縑於度支取直，吏私增賈厚給之，經用益耗。

translations.literal: Initially, the Shence Army mostly submitted silk claim certificates to the Bureau of Public Revenue to receive cash payment; clerks privately inflated prices and gave generous payment, so routine expenditures grew ever more depleted.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Shence Army had largely drawn cash from the Bureau of Public Revenue in exchange for silk allotments; clerks privately inflated prices and paid generously, steadily draining routine funds.

sentences.zh: 開成初，有詔禁止。

translations.literal: Early in Kaicheng, an edict forbade this.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng reign an edict forbade the practice.

sentences.zh: 時宦者仇士良、魚弘誌方用事，彥威乃奏復與直，悅媚士良等。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs Qiu Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi were in power; Yanwei memorialized to restore cash payment, to please and flatter Qiu Shiliang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs Qiu Shiliang and Yu Hongzhi then held power; Yanwei memorialized to restore cash payments — a move calculated to please them.

sentences.zh: 又效王播貢羨贏以冀速進。

translations.literal: Again he imitated Wang Bo in presenting surplus tribute to hope for rapid advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He also copied Wang Bo's tactic of presenting surplus revenue to the throne in hopes of rapid promotion.

sentences.zh: 會邊兵訴所賜不時，縑皆敝惡，攝吏送臺獄，而彥威視事自如，及詔停務，始惶恐就第。

translations.literal: It happened that frontier soldiers complained that what was granted was not timely and the silk was all worn and shoddy; acting officials sent them to the censorate prison, while Yanwei conducted business as usual; only when an edict ordered suspension of duties did he at last flee in fear to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier soldiers then complained that disbursements were late and the silk shoddy; acting officials had them sent to censorate prison while Yanwei carried on as though nothing were amiss. Only when an edict suspended his duties did he flee in alarm to his residence.

sentences.zh: 貶衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was demoted to chamberlain for the imperial stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Chamberlain for the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校禮部尚書，為忠武節度使，毀山房三千餘所，盜無所容。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting minister of rites and made military commissioner of Zhongwu; he destroyed more than three thousand mountain dens, and bandits had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting Minister of Rites and military commissioner of Zhongwu, where he destroyed more than three thousand mountain hideouts and left bandits nowhere to shelter.

sentences.zh: 徙節宣武，封北海縣子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command Xuanyou and enfeoffed as Viscount of Beihai county.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command Xuanyou and enfeoffed as Viscount of Beihai County.

sentences.zh: 性強敏，善著書，頗行於時。

translations.literal: By nature he was forceful and keen; skilled at writing books, his works circulated widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Forceful and quick-witted, he was a prolific author whose works enjoyed wide currency in his day.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰靖。

translations.literal: Upon death he was posthumously given the post of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with the posthumous title Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：韓愈稱：「郡邑通得祀社稷、孔子。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Han Yu stated: "Commanderies and districts generally may sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain and to Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Han Yu observed, "Every commandery and district may sacrifice at the altars of soil and grain — and to Confucius.

sentences.zh: 獨孔子用王者事，以門人為配，天子以下，北面拜跪薦祭，禮如親弟子者。

translations.literal: Only for Confucius were rites of a king employed, with his disciples as associates; from the Son of Heaven downward, all faced north, bowing and kneeling to present offerings — rites as for one's own disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Only Confucius was honored with the rites due a king, his disciples placed as ritual associates; from the Son of Heaven downward, all faced north, bowing and kneeling to offer sacrifice — the ceremony accorded to one's own disciples.

sentences.zh: 句龍、棄以功，孔子則以德，固自有次第。」

translations.literal: Goulong and Qi were honored for merit; Confucius for virtue — naturally there was an order of precedence."
translations.idiomatic: Goulong and Hou Ji were honored for merit; Confucius for virtue — a clear order of precedence.

sentences.zh: 崇敬乃請東揖，以殺太重。

translations.literal: Chongjing then requested the eastern bow, on grounds that the rites were too weighty in severity.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjing then petitioned that officials bow facing east instead, arguing that the full ritual was excessively solemn.

sentences.zh: 方是時，公卿無韓愈之賢，無有折其非是者。

translations.literal: At that time among high ministers there was none with Han Yu's worth; none refuted his error or rightness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time no minister possessed Han Yu's stature; none stepped forward to challenge Chongjing's proposal.

sentences.zh: 道州刺史薛伯高嘗謂：「夫子稱顏回為庶幾，其從於陳、蔡者，亦各有號，出於一時，後世坐祀十人以為哲，豈夫子誌哉？」

translations.literal: Xue Bogao, prefect of Daozhou, once said: "The Master called Yan Hui 'one who nearly attained'; those who followed him through Chen and Cai each also had their titles, arising from that moment — later ages seated ten men for sacrifice as sages; was this the Master's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bogao, prefect of Daozhou, once argued, "The Master called Yan Hui 'one who nearly attained perfection.' Those who followed him through Chen and Cai each bore titles of the moment. Later ages seated ten men in the temple as sages — was that ever the Master's design?

sentences.zh: 觀七十子之賢，未有加於十人，坐而祀之，始於開元，非特牽於一時之稱號。

translations.literal: Considering the worth of the seventy disciples, none surpassed the ten; seated for sacrifice — this began in the Kaiyuan era, not merely bound to titles of a single moment."
translations.idiomatic: Of the Master's seventy disciples, none surpassed those ten; their seated place in the temple began in Kaiyuan — not a mere attachment to passing titles."

sentences.zh: 《記》曰：「祭，有其舉之，莫敢廢也。」

translations.literal: The Record states: "In sacrifice, what has once been instituted, none dare abolish.
translations.idiomatic: The Record states, "In sacrifice, what has once been instituted, none dare abolish.

sentences.zh: 如崇敬誠不知禮，尊君以媚世，歷朝循而不改矣。

translations.literal: If Chongjing truly did not know ritual, he honored the ruler to flatter the age — successive dynasties have followed without change."
translations.idiomatic: If Chongjing truly knew nothing of ritual, he debased the rites to flatter his age — and every dynasty since has followed suit without alteration.

sentences.zh: 伯高之語，柳宗元誌之於其書，必有辨其妄者。

translations.literal: Bogao's words were recorded by Liu Zongyuan in his book; surely there were those who distinguished and refuted its error.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zongyuan recorded Bogao's argument in his works; surely someone must have answered its folly.
